item.title: Le suspect de l'attaque dans les Yvelines placé en observation psychiatrique
item.description: Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le suspect de l'attaque commise vendredi dans les Yvelines, qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés graves, dont une fillette de 12 ans, a été placé en observation psychiatrique, le temps d'apprécier si son état de santé est compatible avec la poursuite des auditions, a annoncé dimanche le parquet national antiterroriste (PNAT). Ce placement en observation psychiatrique peut durer 48 heures et la garde à vue du suspect est suspendue durant cette période, a précisé le PNAT. Une analyse toxicologique a en outre permis de révéler la présence de cannabis et de cocaïne dans le sang de cet homme, a ajouté le PNAT. Les gardes à vue des membres de son entourage familial et amical se poursuivent. A la suite de cette attaque contre des passants commise à l'aide d'une arme automatique, le PNAT a ouvert une enquête du chef de "tentatives d'assassinats en relation avec une entreprise terroriste, avec la circonstance que les faits ont été commis à raison de l’appartenance vraie ou supposée, à une prétendue race, une ethnie, une nation ou une religion déterminée". Le président de la République Emmanuel Macron a qualifié cette attaque d'"attentat terroriste" à "caractère raciste avéré".

item.title: Jordan church attack survivor says her cousin died before her eyes
item.description: When gunmen began opening fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screamed in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
item.content:encoded: When gunmen began opening fire on a church in Jordan, Sahar al-Halsa hid behind a pillar as she heard the shooting and people screamed in panic during a funeral service for her cousin's daughter. When she rushed outside in the chaos, she said she spotted the assailants and another cousin lying on the ground wounded. "I went to him and said: 'Assem, Assem, my darling, answer me'," she said. She said he opened his eyes to look at her, but then "he was gone". Friday's attack on the Greek Orthodox place of worship in Karak governorate, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman, prompted King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, to order security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to what authorities described as extremist terrorism. PRIEST SENDS MESSAGE OF LOVE AND PEACE Nine people died in the shooting that witnesses said lasted for several minutes. Their funeral service is expected on Sunday. Forty people were wounded in the rare attack on minority Christians. Speaking from her home, from where the red dome of St George's church is visible, al-Halsa concluded that God must have saved her. "My life starts now, because I was going to die," she said, speaking beside her husband Ziad al-Halsa. A statue of Jesus on a cross was displayed on a shelf. Authorities have said they are still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There has been no immediate claim of responsibility. Sahar's husband Ziad said he ran the short distance to the church after he heard the gunfire, describing the overwhelming sense of relief when he realised Sahar, who he described as "the love of his life", was safe. "To my cousins, may God have mercy on them," he said. Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities there say they have foiled several Islamist plots in recent years. Speaking ahead of the funerals, priest Yuhanna Hamati said: "Our message from this church, from this place where this horrific crime was committed, is a message of love, peace, and reassurance. A message that we send to the whole world."

item.title: Employees group warns of major Swiss job losses if UBS relocates, newspaper says
item.description: As many as 12,000 UBS jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association (SBPV), newspaper NZZ am Sonntag reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: As many as 12,000 UBS (UBSG.S) jobs in Switzerland could be at risk if tougher capital rules prompt the bank to relocate, according to the Swiss Bank Employees Association (SBPV), newspaper NZZ am Sonntag reported. • In a letter to lawmakers cited by the paper, the SBPV warned a relocation could cost 10,000 to 12,000 of UBS's roughly 34,000 jobs in Switzerland, on top of cuts already under way as it completes its integration of fallen rival Credit Suisse. • Neither UBS nor the SBPV immediately replied to requests from Reuters for comment. • The warning comes as a committee in the lower house of the Swiss parliament [USN:L1N45N0NB TEXT:"prepares"] to discuss how much capital UBS should have to hold to back its foreign subsidiaries. • Last month, the upper house [USN:L8N45F0DE TEXT:"proposed"] UBS should back those units with 90% Common Equity Tier 1 capital. • UBS has suggested that is [USN:L1N45C05I TEXT:"too much"] and the bank's chairman has warned it would need to carefully [USN:L8N4590WE TEXT:"consider"] its future in Switzerland if the new rules are too harsh. • Some shareholders of the bank have called for UBS to [USN:L1N45N061 TEXT:"leave"] Switzerland, and the bank has been [USN:L1N46205Q TEXT:"drafting"] potential contingency plans including shifting its headquarters or merging with another lender, sources have told Reuters. • In its letter, the SBPV called for a "viable compromise", saying stricter capital requirements could call into question UBS remaining based in Switzerland.

item.title: Clinical Catlin triumphs in Hong Kong Open
item.description: American John Catlin showed nerves of steel as he held local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finnish opponent Kalle Samooja at bay to win the Hong Kong Open, hitting seven birdies in Sunday's final round to finish five strokes ahead of his nearest challengers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: American John Catlin showed nerves of steel as he held local favourite Matthew Cheung and Finnish opponent Kalle Samooja at bay to win the Hong Kong Open, hitting seven birdies in Sunday's final round to finish five strokes ahead of his nearest challengers. Catlin, who won the Asian Tour Order of Merit in 2024, hit a six-under 64 in the fourth round to finish 20-under, earning his seventh title on the tour. Samooja led Cheung by a stroke going into the tricky 18th hole, but hit a bogey and had to settle for a joint second-place finish, as the latter secured the best finish for a Hong Kong player at the tournament in Fanling. "It's very, very special. Any time you can be on a trophy with some of the greatest players that ever played the game, I just feel very humble and very grateful," said Catlin. The 35-year-old was jointly leading the scoreboard along with Thomas Pieters and Caleb Surratt after the third round, where Cheung slipped from the top with three bogeys on Saturday. A clinical Catlin shook off a bogey on the fifth hole to take a solo lead on Sunday, and quickly fixed a mistake on the 14th as he found the centre of the green with a precise 120-yard stroke from thick grass to stay on course for a birdie. Error-prone Pieters and Surratt finished tied for sixth place with Sampson Zheng. Catlin's first trophy on the Asian Tour since April 2024 also earned him an invitation to next year's Open Championship and a maiden qualification for the Masters. "It's like a dream come true... it's been a long time coming, lot of hard work, lot of times when you weren't sure what was coming but you just kind of held the faith and I just kept working," Catlin said, shaking his head. "To finally be at the Masters, speechless."

item.title: Brookfield builds Qatar presence with Doha office

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alternative asset manager Brookfield (BAM.N) said on Sunday it had opened an office in Doha anchored by its global credit platform as it deepens its presence in Qatar and expands across the Gulf region. The Doha office will be anchored by Brookfield's global credit platform, including Oaktree, underscoring the growing role of private credit in financing Gulf economies The move deepens Brookfield's exposure to Qatar, including a $20 billion AI infrastructure investment programme with a QIA-backed AI company [USN:L4N3XF0P6 TEXT:"Qai"] Establishing a local presence gives Brookfield closer access to sovereign wealth funds, institutional investors and deal opportunities in what has been one of the region's fastest-growing investment markets Brookfield is the latest global investment firm to establish a presence in Qatar as asset managers expand local teams to capture investment opportunities across the Gulf One of the world's largest LNG exporters before the war, Qatar is trying to diversify its economy away from energy and attract foreign investment

item.title: NHL roundup: Leafs erupt in third, rout Oilers for fourth straight win
item.description: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday. Jack Roslovic recorded a goal and an assist, while Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored and Kirill Marchenko nabbed two assists. For Edmonton, Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard had two helpers each. Anthony Stolarz stopped 30 shots for his fourth victory as Toronto posted its first four-game win streak since January. Tristan Jarry turned away 25 shots for the Oilers, who had won three in a row. With his 11th and 12th goals of the season, Draisaitl shares the NHL lead with the Minnesota Wild's Kirill Kaprizov. Draisaitl is second in the league in scoring with 23 points -- 10 shy of McDavid, who has eight goals and a league-leading 25 assists. Mammoth 5, Lightning 4 (OT) Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting Utah past Tampa Bay in Salt Lake City. Simashev slipped in a pass from Barrett Hayton at 1:44 for his first career game-winner. Utah also received goals from Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee. Vincent Trocheck had two assists. Mammoth goaltender Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves and earned the secondary assist on Simashev's winner. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg, Brayden Point and Conor Geekie hit the net for the Lightning, and Dennis Hildeby made 23 saves. Nikita Kucherov collected an assist for his 1,138th career point, passing Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead. Blue Jackets 2, Golden Knights 1 (OT) Adam Fantilli scored a power-play goal 59 seconds into overtime to lead Columbus to a victory over visiting Vegas. It was Fantilli's third goal of the season and snapped a 0-for-22 drought on the power play for the Blue Jackets. Denton Mateychuk also scored a goal, Kent Johnson added two assists and Cam Talbot finished with 26 saves. Tomas Hertl scored for Vegas and Hart stopped 18 of 20 shots for Vegas, which saw its losing streak extended to a season-high three games. The Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal in five straight games. Penguins 3, Predators 2 (OT) Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for ailing Pittsburgh, which rallied to take down visiting Nashville. Connor Dewar and Rickard Rakell also scored for the Penguins, who won their second straight game. Arturs Silovs finished with 24 saves, marking the first time the team has won consecutive games since starting the season 2-0. Steven Stamkos scored his fifth of the season and Jayden Struble notched his first for the Predators, who are 0-4 in overtime and shootouts. Juuse Saros made a season-high 34 saves, but Rakell spoiled his bid for a victory by tying the game with 1:06 remaining in regulation. Bruins 6, Sharks 4 Boston scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, to edge visiting San Jose and run its unbeaten streak to eight games. David Pastrnak tied former teammate Patrice Bergeron for third on Boston's all-time goals list (427) to kick off the late-game surge. Fraser Minten (game-winner), James Hagens and Casey Mittelstadt all had a goal and an assist, while Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka each dished out two assists, and Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves. Michael Misa, Kiefer Sherwood, Dmitry Orlov and Will Smith each scored a goal, Jacob Trouba had two assists, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 shots for the Sharks, who were on a two-game win streak. Ducks 5, Flyers 4 Tristan Luneau had a goal and two assists as visiting Anaheim snapped a five-game losing streak with a victory over Philadelphia. Leo Carlsson chipped in with a goal and an assist against the team that signed him to a five-year, $90 million offer sheet over the summer. Anaheim ultimately matched the deal, making the 21-year-old the highest paid player in the league. Beckett Sennecke and A.J. Greer also scored and Lukas Dostal turned aside 28 shots. Matvei Michkov scored his seventh and eighth goals for Philadelphia, which had won three straight since losing its first nine. Porter Martone had a goal and an assist and Tyson Foerster also scored, while Trevor Zegras recorded two assists against his former team. Joseph Woll finished with 21 saves. Devils 3, Kings 1 Arseny Gritsyuk scored for the fifth straight game to help New Jersey seal a win against Los Angeles in Newark, N.J. Anthony Mantha and Brett Pesce also scored, and Jake Allen made 12 saves for New Jersey, which has won three straight and five of the past six. Scott Laughton scored and Anton Forsberg made 23 saves for the Kings, who had won two in a row following a 0-4-2 start to the season. Senators 7, Rangers 4 Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as Ottawa topped visiting New York. Jake Sanderson tallied one goal and added two assists, while Dylan Cozens and Michael Amadio each scored and chipped in a helper. Tim Stutzle also found the back of the net as Ottawa improved to 5-2-0 on home ice. Jonas Johansson, making his Senators and season debut, made 24 saves. J.T. Miller and Will Cuylle each scored and added an assist, and Alexis Lafreniere and Pavel Dorofeyev also scored for the Rangers, who are 1-3-1 in their last five. Adam Fox and Noah Laba each added a pair of helpers, and Dylan Garand stopped 17 shots. Hurricanes 4, Blues 0 Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves to lead Carolina to a road victory over St. Louis. Sean Walker, Jesperi Kotkaniemi, Logan Stankoven, and Nikolaj Ehlers all lit the lamp as the Hurricanes closed out their five-game road trip with a victory and a 3-2-0 record. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis each picked up a pair of assists, while Joel Hofer finished with 35 saves in the losing effort. Wild 5, Kraken 1 Kirill Kaprizov scored his 12th goal of the season -- tying for the league lead -- and added an assist as Minnesota dominated host Seattle. Kaprizov, who is tied for first in goals with the Edmonton Oilers' Leon Draisaitl, opened the scoring on a breakaway just 26 seconds into the game. Blake Coleman scored twice, including an empty-netter with 3:36 remaining, while Joel Eriksson Ek added a goal and an assist and Olli Maatta also tallied. Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves. Berkly Catton scored for the Kraken, who had won their previous two games. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 shots. Capitals 4, Sabres 3 Alex Tuch scored his second goal of the game at 3:42 of overtime to lift host Washington to victory over Buffalo, his former team. Tuch, acquired by Washington in a sign-and-trade deal with Buffalo in June, was in the slot to take a pass from Dylan Strome behind the net and beat a screened Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen inside the left post. Strome also scored twice, and Charlie Lindgren made 18 saves for the Capitals. Jack Quinn, Josh Doan and Noah Ostlund scored for the Sabres, who built a 2-0 lead halfway through the first period. Luukkonen made 30 saves. Flames 4, Red Wings 1 Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as Calgary cruised past visiting Detroit, snapping the Red Wings' eight-game winning streak in the series. Matvei Gridin had a goal and an assist for the Flames, while Ryan Strome and Zayne Parekh also scored. Matt Coronato added two assists. Devin Cooley made 28 saves for Calgary, which has won three straight and four of their last five games after opening the season with five consecutive losses. Andrew Copp scored the lone goal for Detroit, which had won three of its previous four games. John Gibson made 21 saves after leaving his previous start Thursday because of an eye issue. --Field Level Media

item.title: Russie-Trois morts dans des attaques dans la région de Belgorod
item.description: Deux personnes ont été tuées et 13 autres blessées dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche par une attaque de drone ukrainienne contre la ville de Belgorod, en Russie, près de la frontière entre les deux pays, ont déclaré les autorités locales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deux personnes ont été tuées et 13 autres blessées dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche par une attaque de drone ukrainienne contre la ville de Belgorod, en Russie, près de la frontière entre les deux pays, ont déclaré les autorités locales. "L'attaque a endommagé 30 ensembles d'appartements, 35 voitures, quatre maisons, trois bâtiments administratifs, huit locaux commerciaux et trois installations sociales", a dit le gouverneur de la région de Belgorod, Alexandre Chouvaïev. Une troisième personne a été tuée et une autre blessée dans un village près de la ville de Chebekino, ont dit les autorités.

item.title: Russia says it hit a cargo vessel and Ukrainian logistic hubs overnight
item.description: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk during an overnight attack.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk during an overnight attack. The ministry said the vessel was being used to supply the Ukrainian army. Russian forces also hit a logistics centre, a distribution centre and a logistics terminal in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv. The ministry said the facilities had been used for storage and distribution of dual-use cargo for the Ukrainian military. Reuters could not independently verify the Defence Ministry's information.

item.title: Three people killed and 14 injured in Ukrainian attacks on Russia's Belgorod region, governor says
item.description: An overnight Ukrainian drone attack on the city of Belgorod near the Russian border with Ukraine killed two people and injured 13, local authorities said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An overnight Ukrainian drone attack on the city of Belgorod near the Russian border with Ukraine killed two people and injured 13, local authorities said on Sunday. "The attack has damaged 30 blocks of flats, 35 cars, four houses, three administrative buildings, eight commercial premises and three social facilities," said Belgorod regional governor Alexander Shuvayev. Another person was killed and one was injured in a village near the town of Shebekino, authorities said.

item.title: Drone attack injures five people, damages industrial facility in Russia’s Perm region, governor says
item.description: A drone attack on Russia's Perm region damaged an industrial facility, injuring five of its workers, regional governor Dmitry Makhonin said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A drone attack on Russia's Perm region damaged an industrial facility, injuring five of its workers, regional governor Dmitry Makhonin said on Sunday. Emergency services were at the scene and that the injured people received the necessary medical help, he said on the state-backed MAX messaging app without providing further detail on the nature of the damage.

item.title: Saudi, Egyptian stocks sink as Yemen conflict intensifies
item.description: Saudi and Egyptian bourses fell on Sunday after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted drones and missiles over Riyadh and southern regions as fighting with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensified.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi and Egyptian bourses fell on Sunday after the Saudi-led [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"coalition said"] it had intercepted drones and missiles over Riyadh and southern regions as fighting with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensified. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) dropped 2.6%, pressured by broad-based selling as investors assessed the risk of the Yemen conflict becoming a broader front in the regional war. The index is on track to log its worst intraday performance since April 2025, with heavyweight Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) falling 1.1%. Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) tumbled 2.5%, eyeing its lowest level in nearly seven months, with all of its constituents in negative territory. Egypt's parliament is expected to vote on October 26 on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia, if requested, in its conflict with Yemen's Houthis. The voting was initially scheduled for October 20.
