item.title: NBA roundup: Nikola Jokic records 199th triple-double, Nuggets top Pels
item.description: Nikola Jokic recorded 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray poured in 42 points and the Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to top the visiting New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nikola Jokic recorded 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray poured in 42 points and the Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to top the visiting New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night. Jokic has 199 career regular-season triple-doubles in 12 seasons, second to just-retired Russell Westbrook's 209 in 18 seasons starting in 2008-09. Trevon Brazile scored seven of his 17 points in overtime and hit a corner 3-pointer late in the extra period, Christian Braun had 15 points in the game and DeMar DeRozan added 12 points for the Nuggets. Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22, Zion Williamson and Derik Queen contributed 17 each, Saddiq Bey scored 14 and Jeremiah Fears added 10. Hornets 115, Heat 110 Brandon Miller pumped in 34 points and Charlotte recovered from blowing a 23-point lead to beat visiting Miami. Dennis Schroder added 25 points, Naz Reid scored 23 and Grayson Allen contributed 20. Miller was the only one of the Hornets' top four scorers who played for the team last season. Davion Mitchell's 22 points and 10 assists paced the Heat, who remained winless through three games despite erasing a 23-point deficit to tie the score at 100. Bam Adebayo's 20 points and eight rebounds gave Miami a lift, Pelle Larsson supplied 15 points, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson each had 14, and Bobby Portis scored 13. Cavaliers 125, Nets 121 Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as Cleveland built a 22-point lead before holding on for a victory over visiting Brooklyn. Evan Mobley added 20 points and 10 rebounds, and Jaylon Tyson scored 15 points off the bench in the Cavaliers' home opener. James Harden collected 12 points, eight rebounds and seven assists as Cleveland picked up its first win. Brooklyn, which trailed 104-82 with 9:29 remaining, pulled within 123-121 on Michael Porter Jr.'s 3-pointer with 8.1 seconds left. Porter (28 points, nine rebounds) fouled out on the subsequent possession and Sam Merrill hit two free throws to put the Cavaliers up four with 5.2 seconds remaining. Julius Randle had 23 points for winless Brooklyn. 76ers 127, Bucks 116 Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead Philadelphia to a home win over Milwaukee. Embiid finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for the 76ers, who rested LeBron James (back/sciatica). James is expected to play Sunday against the Detroit Pistons, while Embiid will rest in the second half of a back-to-back. Tyrese Maxey pitched in with 26 points, while VJ Edgecombe delivered a 17-point, 13-rebound effort. While Philadelphia is 3-0 on the young season, the Bucks fell to 0-3 despite eight players scoring in double figures. Jaime Jaquez Jr. led Milwaukee with 21 points, while Kel'el Ware had 19 points and 13 rebounds off the bench for the visitors. Wizards 124, Bulls 120 Trae Young paired 25 points with nine assists and Kyshawn George added 22 points and nine rebounds as Washington downed host Chicago to open a three-game road trip. The Wizards outscored the Bulls 40-20 in the third quarter. Anthony Davis and Young combined to go 6-for-6 from the free-throw line to hold onto the lead. Davis (19 points) and Tre Johnson (13) also scored in double figures for Washington, while Justin Champagnie had an 11-point, 14-rebound double-double. Chicago rookie Caleb Wilson contributed 30 points and 14 rebounds for his first career double-double, and teammate Matas Buzelis scored 21 points. Norman Powell added 18, Jalen Smith had 14 and Tre Jones 10. Josh Giddey had nine points, 10 assists and eight rebounds. Suns 131, Warriors 122 Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and host Phoenix won to send Golden State to its worst start in almost two decades. Miles Bridges scored 16 points and Dillon Brooks added 15 points for the Suns, who won their home opener. Booker set a franchise record for points in a home opener. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 points and nine rebounds and De'Anthony Melton scored 25 points for the Warriors, who fell to 0-3 for the first time since 2007-08. Golden State was without starters Stephen Curry (knee), Brandin Podziemski (back) and Draymond Green (back) and reserve Al Horford (back). Spurs 122, Mavericks 106 Victor Wembanyama scored 23 points as visiting San Antonio earned its first win of the season by defeating short-handed Dallas in the second of a back-to-back for both teams. Dylan Harper added 22 points, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle scored 19 each, Julian Champagnie hit for 12 off the bench and Devin Vassell tallied 11 points for the Spurs. Wembanyama also posted seven rebounds and four blocks. The Mavericks played without stars Cooper Flagg (shoulder) and Kyrie Irving, who was held out for left knee injury management. Flagg sprained his left shoulder in a win at Indiana on Friday and will be reevaluated next week. Rookie Sergio De Larrea's 21 points led Dallas. Marcus Sasser, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford scored 12 apiece. Rockets 121, Hawks 114 Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as Houston topped host Atlanta to improve to 3-0. The Rockets also got 19 points apiece from Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard, who started in place of Fred VanVleet (right knee load management). Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each scored 17 points, with Sengun grabbing 10 rebounds and Thompson collecting 11. The Hawks were led by Jalen Johnson, who fell just shy of a triple-double with 26 points, 16 assists and nine rebounds. Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels scored 18 points apiece, and CJ McCollum added 17. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brazil heads to polls in runoff between leftist Lula and Bolsonaro Jr.
item.description: A victory for Flavio Bolsonaro would extend a wave of right-wing victories for Latin American candidates friendly to US President Donald Trump, while a fourth mandate for Lula would be a disappointment in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin
item.content:encoded: Brazilians head to the polls on Sunday in a tight runoff vote that could shift Latin America's largest nation sharply rightward, bringing it closer to the United States as part of a broader conservative shift across the region. The runoff pits leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro. Flavio scored [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"a major upset at the start of the month"] by defying pollsters to lead voting in the first round. A victory for Bolsonaro, 45, would extend a wave of right-wing victories for Latin American candidates friendly to US President Donald Trump, while a fourth mandate for Lula would be a disappointment in Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security. The election race has been dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling, which Washington denies. It has also been colored by fallout from [USN:L1N43T0Q4 TEXT:"Jair Bolsonaro's 2025"] conviction for plotting a 2022 coup, with Flavio pledging to free his father if he is elected. Trump has called the case a "witch hunt" and imposed a 50% tariff on Brazil in 2025, in a decision explicitly linked to Jair Bolsonaro’s trial. While many of those were later watered down, Trump unleashed [USN:L1N43P1HE TEXT:"new levies against Brazil this year"], citing unfair trade practices. Lula has cast the Trump administration’s proximity to the Bolsonaro clan as part of an attempt to sway the election, while labeling tariffs and other punitive measures as bullying. On economic issues, despite falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over an electorate grappling with high living costs and heavy household debt. Endemic gang violence also weighs on voters’ minds. Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns and has also promised a heavy-handed approach to fighting crime, pledging maximum-security jails and chemical castration for serious sexual offenses. CANDIDATES ARE NECK AND NECK Polls show the candidates are practically tied going into the runoff, as Lula has closed the gap in the final days. Historical precedent favors Bolsonaro, however, as no candidate has ever won the presidency after coming second in the first-round vote. Bolsonaro picked up 47% of ballots cast in the first round, while Lula trailed with 45%. The senator's first-round win [USN:L6N45Q08A TEXT:"sent Brazil's markets and currency soaring"] on expectations of pro-business reforms. His first-round success was mirrored in congressional elections for his Liberal Party and other right-wing politicians, which could pave a legislative path for him, or complicate governance for Lula.

item.title: Disenchanted Netanyahu supporters are prize of Israel election campaign
item.description: Opinion polls for months have predicted Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties losing its majority. But his top rival, centrist Gadi Eisenkot, has no clear path to power either.
item.dc:creator: Emily Rose, Maayan Lubell
item.content:encoded: In the remote Negev Desert town of Dimona, long a bastion of Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party, disenchanted voters are going door-to-door campaigning for his top rival, hoping to bring down the veteran prime minister in Israel's election on Tuesday. The ballot is Israel's first since Hamas' October 7, 2023, surprise attack that shook the country and plunged the region into turmoil, as Israel went to war on the militant group in Gaza and its allies in Lebanon and Iran. The October 7 security breach saw Likud's popularity plummet. Opinion polls for months have predicted Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties losing its majority. But his top rival, centrist Gadi Eisenkot, has no clear path to power either, and the race has become tighter as the election nears. Dimona, where an Iranian missile wounded dozens in March, has become a political battleground. "We must have change. Bibi has to go," said Yossi Assayag, 74, who says he has supported Likud most his life. "Bibi has brought disaster to Israel." LIKUD LOYALISTS Assayag is part of a cohort of town residents trying to convince their community to vote for Eisenkot's party Yashar, which is neck-and-neck with Likud in the polls. It's a tough task in Dimona, where half the voters in the previous 2022 election cast a ballot for Likud. "I will never betray Likud," said Ruti Ohana, a pensioner, who says she has voted Likud ever since immigrating to Israel from North Africa more than 60 years ago. She said Netanyahu was a cut above his rivals, and the blame he receives from detractors for October 7 was unfair. Right-wing Likud long ago formed a core voter base among Jews of Middle Eastern and North African descent, known as Mizrahis, who felt neglected by the European-influenced centre-left Labor Party that dominated Israel for generations. Labor has since dwindled to a rump as Israeli politics have shifted rightwards, and there are now around half a dozen other parties courting Likud voters, from the centre to the far right. But the link to the party among its past supporters remains strong. "Most people here vote for Likud just because that's how they were raised," said Oria Asaf, 25, a past Likud voter now backing Yashar. "The change will come when people start to think about their children's future rather than their parents' past." BATTLE FOR WAVERING LIKUDNIKS While Netanyahu has a hard core of supporters that can't be won over, the prize is undecided voters who "understand that we are in a state of crisis" and are open to persuasion, said Michal Elmalem Abu, elected as a member of the city council from Likud and now leading Eisenkot's Dimona campaign. Some 13% of Israeli voters have yet to decide how they will vote, according to data collected by the Viterbi Family Center for Public Opinion and Policy Research at the Israel Democracy Institute. Of those who voted for Likud in 2022, just 55% now say they will vote for the party again on Tuesday. Fifteen percent will support parties aligned against Netanyahu, including 8% for Yashar. Another 14% will vote for alternative right-wing parties, and 9% are undecided. It is in places just like Dimona where Eisenkot stands a chance to bite a chunk out of Likud's base, said Amotz Asa-El, a political scientist at the Hartman Institute. A child of Moroccan immigrants who rose through the ranks to become military chief of staff, Eisenkot, 66, has a personal story of humble origins from the Mizrahi community that "appeals to a big swath of the Israeli electorate, particularly Likud's traditional electorate", said Asa-El. In an electoral field crowded with ex-soldiers, his peerless security credentials are an asset. The loss of his son, killed in combat in Gaza in December 2023, resonates with voters. At a town hall during a visit to Dimona in July, residents said they were excited about the prospect of a leader of Mizrahi descent. Others approached him with hugs and tearful condolences for the loss of his son. But a week later Netanyahu held his own event, demonstrating his powerful appeal in the hardscrabble Negev, where Likud governments have long boasted of bringing development funds. "Look around you, look at your community, look at what was here then and what is here now, and ask yourselves which governments invested in this monumental effort. And I do this out of immense love," he said. Lior Katzav, a Likud former mayor of Kiryat Malachi, another small-town stronghold, said party surveys show voters who had abandoned Likud are returning as the election nears. But even some who are sympathetic to Netanyahu say it may be time for a change. Israel's youngest prime minister when he was first elected 30 years ago, he has since become its longest-serving, now 77, having governed for 18 years over six terms. "It's time for him to go," said Dimona software engineer David Iskali. "He's done a lot for Israel but it can't go on. I won't give my vote to someone almost 80-years-old."

item.title: World Series rematch, Indian edition: Yankees beat Dodgers in Mumbai event
item.description: Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to.
item.dc:creator: Revathi Hariharan
item.content:encoded: Mumbai's cricket fans packed the stands at the Andheri Sports Complex on Saturday to watch Indian World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav swing a bat - just not the kind that they are used to. Indian cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar and Radha Yadav lined up alongside ex-Major League Baseball players Nick Swisher, Adrian Gonzalez, Jake Arrieta and Jonny Gomes in a three-on-three tournament that organisers pitched as a bridge between the two bat-and-ball games. Each of the four teams mixed a baseball veteran, an Indian cricketer and an American softball player and the scoring rewarded both muscle and precision. A home run earned two points, hitting the target zone earned four and fielders picked up one point for a catch, while five consecutive out-of-the-park hits doubled a team's total. The semifinals offered up both a thriller and a stroll, as Gonzalez's Los Angeles Dodgers overturned the Shardul-led Chicago Cubs' 44 runs with just a minute to spare, while Suryakumar's New York Yankees cruised past the Boston Red Sox. That set up a rematch of the 2024 World Series, this time in India, with the Yankees posting 78 and holding off the Dodgers to be crowned champions. Softball player Rachel Garcia was named the tournament's most valuable player. Suryakumar, a former India captain who guided the side to victory at this year's Twenty20 Cricket World Cup on home soil, said he is confident baseball will grow in India and that cricketing skills can translate to success in the American sport. "I think it's all about good range hitting," added Suryakumar, whose celebrations spilled into the stands as he placed the gold chain he won around his wife's neck after the win. "You must be strong from head to your lower body, have a good core and strong arms. If you want to hit 450 feet, 500 feet, you got to be strong. Work hard. No substitutes."

item.title: Borr Drilling rig sinks off Gabon, five personnel missing
item.description: Borr Drilling's Prospector 5 drilling rig sank during jacking operations off the coast of Gabon as it prepared for a drilling campaign, with 5 of the 115 people on board unaccounted for, the company said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Borr Drilling's (BORR.N) Prospector 5 drilling rig sank during jacking operations off the coast of Gabon as it prepared for a drilling campaign, with 5 of the 115 people on board unaccounted for, the company said on Sunday. "Preliminary information indicates that the rig experienced a punch-through event during preload activities, resulting in loss of stability and the subsequent sinking of the rig," the offshore drilling contractor said. The Prospector 5 oil and gas rig, owned and operated by Borr, is contracted to support BW Energy's (BWE.OL) drilling operations off Gabon, it said. "We are deeply concerned for those who remain unaccounted for and everyone affected by this incident," said Borr Drilling Chief Executive Bruno Morand. "Our immediate priority is supporting the ongoing search and rescue efforts and the welfare of all personnel involved." Panoro Energy (PENR.OL) , which holds a 17.5% stake in the field, said production had been halted, adding that there were no reports of damage or accidental discharges.

item.title: Guadalajara gana de visita en el torneo mexicano de fútbol
item.description: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado 1-0 de visita a Monterrey en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, ganó el sábado 1-0 de visita a Monterrey en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura. Las "Chivas" de Guadalajara llegaron a 26 puntos para mantenerse en el segundo lugar general, por abajo del líder América que registra 27 unidades. En el partido, disputado en el estadio BBVA de Monterrey, Guadalajara anotó el gol del triunfo a los nueve minutos con un disparo cruzado de Roberto "Piojo" Alvarado tras recibir un pase de Santiago Sandoval, quien aprovechó un error defensivo de Víctor Guzmán para robar el balón. Monterrey tuvo la opción de empatar a los 19 minutos con un tiro penal, pero el portero Raúl Rangel atajó el disparo del argentino Lucas Ocampos. Los "Rayados" de Monterrey habían rescatado el empate en tiempo de reposición cuando el balón le rebotó en el pecho a Diego Rossi tras un desvío defensivo, pero el árbitro anuló el gol tras revisar en el VAR la jugada en la que el balón le pegó en la mano al centrocampista uruguayo. "Me gustó mucho el comportamiento del equipo en el aspecto defensivo y el orden que tuvimos para neutralizar a un equipo que cuenta con jugadores de mucho talento, con mucho desequilibrio y, además, muy bien trabajado. Me gustó el esfuerzo colectivo y la garra con la que se jugó el partido, es muy importante que mi equipo juegue con ese espíritu competitivo", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico de Guadalajara, el argentino Gabriel Milito. "Siempre digo que la contundencia es fundamental en el fútbol, encontrar el gol es determinante, pero también es muy importante generar situaciones, peor sería no generarlas, porque si no creas oportunidades es imposible marcar goles. El camino que queda por delante es duro, primero tenemos que terminar el torneo y después vendrá la Liguilla (Postemporada)", agregó. A la postemporada o liguilla clasifican los clubes que ocupan los primeros ocho lugares de la tabla general al final de las 17 jornadas de la temporada regular. En los otros partidos disputados el sábado, Pumas UNAM y Tigres UANL empataron 1-1 con goles del paraguayo Robert Morales y del argentino Juan Francisco Brunetta, respectivamente. León y Toluca empataron 1-1. Para León anotó José Alvarado, mientras que para los "Diablos Rojos" de Toluca lo hizo el uruguayo Federico Viñas. La jornada finalizará el domingo cuando Atlas sea local ante Puebla, el actual campeón Cruz Azul visite a Querétaro, América juegue ante Pachuca y Tijuana sea rival de Santos Laguna. El viernes, Atlético de San Luis ganó de visita al Atlante por 1-0. Por su parte, Necaxa y Bravos de Ciudad Juárez empataron 1-1.

item.title: Kawano, Henderson set world marathon race walk records
item.description: Japan's Masatora Kawano and Australia's Rebecca Henderson set the men's and women's world records for the marathon race walks at the All Japan Race Walking meet in Takahata on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan's Masatora Kawano and Australia's Rebecca Henderson set the men's and women's world records for the marathon race walks at the All Japan Race Walking meet in Takahata on Sunday. Kawano, a two-time world championships medallist in the 35-km event, set the inaugural men’s world record for the distance, with a time of 2:55:14. Henderson improved on Italian [USN:L1N44C02R TEXT:"Sofia Fiorini's record"] from the European Athletics Championships, clocking 3:14:52 at the World Athletics Race Walking Tour Bronze event. The half marathon and marathon became official race walk distances in January this year.

item.title: Flames continue turnaround, top Wings for third straight win
item.description: Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as the Calgary Flames cruised past the visiting Detroit Red Wings 4-1 on Saturday, snapping Detroit's eight-game winning streak in the teams' series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joel Farabee scored a goal and added two assists as the Calgary Flames cruised past the visiting Detroit Red Wings 4-1 on Saturday, snapping Detroit's eight-game winning streak in the teams' series. Matvei Gridin had a goal and an assist for Calgary, while Ryan Strome and Zayne Parekh also scored. Matt Coronato added two assists. Devin Cooley made 28 saves for the Flames, who have won three straight and four of their last five games after opening the season with five consecutive losses. Andrew Copp scored the lone goal for Detroit, which had won three of its previous four games. John Gibson made 21 saves after leaving his previous start Thursday because of an eye issue. Farabee, who extended his point streak to four games with two goals and four assists during that span, put Calgary on the board at 17:50 of the first period. Adam Klapka set him up for a snap shot, while Kevin Bahl also assisted on Farabee's second goal of the season. Copp tied the game at 2:22 of the second period with his second goal of the season. J.T. Compher set him up for a backhand shot past Cooley. Parekh put Calgary back in front at 8:38 with a power-play snap shot for his first goal of the season. Strome extended the lead to 3-1 at 17:04, converting a pass from Morgan Frost for his second goal of the season. Gridin capped the scoring at 18:30 of the second period with a power-play snap shot for his second goal of the campaign. The Flames will look to complete a sweep of their four-game homestand Monday against the Toronto Maple Leafs, while the Red Wings will try to split their four-game road trip Monday against the Edmonton Oilers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australian Grand Prix called off as rain spoils Phillip Island send-off
item.description: The MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather, before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The final Australian MotoGP at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit was called off on Sunday due to heavy rain, ruining the farewell for one of the championship's most beloved circuits. It was a crushing blow for the sold-out crowd [USN:L6N46607H TEXT:"at Phillip Island,"] with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year. The Moto2 and Moto3 races were cancelled first and the MotoGP race was delayed by two hours due to the weather, before organisers threw in the towel and finally called it off at 3:40 p.m. (0440 GMT). "Due to limited visibility affecting the operation of the medical helicopter the MotoGP Grand Prix race has been cancelled," MotoGP said in a statement. "The MotoGP riders will do a lap behind the safety car and stop on the main straight to greet the fans. Pitlane will open for the farewell lap at 15:45 local time." RIDER PARADE The dark clouds and pelting rain brought down the visibility around the circuit, affecting the medical helicopter, which would take 45 minutes to reach the circuit from mainland Melbourne in an emergency. Other than two years lost to the COVID-19 pandemic, the seaside track south of Melbourne had been a fixture on the world championship calendar for 30 years and produced some of Australian motorcycling's most memorable moments. Australian two-times world champion Casey Stoner celebrated six wins in succession from 2007 to 2012, while compatriot Mick Doohan sealed his fifth and final world title with victory in the 1998 race. The raincoat-clad fans who persevered through the rain were treated to a farewell lap from the MotoGP riders, who waved as they slowly made their way around a soaking wet track. Home racer Jack Miller did his best to entertain his supporters with a series of tricks, including a stand-up wheelie over the finish line, before heading over to the grandstand and throwing his gloves and boots into the crowd. MILLER DEJECTED, SIGH OF RELIEF FOR MARTIN The Pramac Racing rider, a very strong performer in the wet, cut a dejected figure when he was interviewed after completing his lap. "This is a tough pill to swallow," said the 31-year-old, who will be leaving MotoGP at the end of the season after more than a decade to join Pata Maxus Yamaha in the World Superbike Championship. "You know, I was praying for rain all weekend. We got the rain, but obviously we weren't organised enough to get the racing going, so it's a tough one. "You guys deserve better. Honestly, all of you have done a fantastic job turning out for Phillip Island, sitting through traffic, sitting through dog-shit weather, all the rest of it. You guys are amazing. Thank you very much." Rain had been expected for the weekend, but MotoGP did not revive its 2023 strategy for the circuit, when the Grand Prix was moved ahead to Saturday and the sprint scheduled for Sunday. That sprint race three years ago was eventually called off. The cancellation of the race also ended the opportunity for seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez to extend his lead in the championship standings, with his title rival Martin declared unfit to compete in the race after [USN:L1N46A017 TEXT:"fracturing his wrist."] Martin held the championship lead heading into the weekend but finds himself 10 points behind Marquez after failing to finish Saturday's sprint after a gruesome crash. On Sunday, Martin's team Aprilia said he would not travel back to Spain to undergo treatment, however, boosting the 2024 champion's hopes of racing at next week's Malaysian Grand Prix and remaining in the title fight.

item.title: Devin Booker, Suns continue Warriors' rough start to season
item.description: Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and the host Phoenix Suns beat Golden State 131-122 on Saturday to send the Warriors to their worst start in almost two decades.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Devin Booker had 43 points, seven assists and seven rebounds and the host Phoenix Suns beat Golden State 131-122 on Saturday to send the Warriors to their worst start in almost two decades. Miles Bridges scored 16 points and Dillon Brooks added 15 points for the Suns, who won their home opener after suffering a 41-point defeat at Portland in their season opener Wednesday. Booker set a franchise record for points in a home opener. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 points and nine rebounds and De'Anthony Melton scored 20 of his 25 points in the second half for the skeleton-crew Warriors, who fell to 0-3 for the first time since 2007-08, when they lost their first six before finishing 48-34. Golden State, playing the second of a back-to-back, was without starters Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski and Draymond Green and reserve Al Horford. Curry (knee), Podziemski (back) and Horford (back) were held out for injury management. Green missed with low back soreness. Brandon Williams added 20 points for the Warriors, who blew a 12-point lead in the final four minutes of a 111-108 home loss to Memphis on Friday. Lendeborg made six of the Warriors' 17 3-pointers on Saturday. Melton had four. Melton scored 13 points in the third quarter, when the Warriors used a 12-0 run to take a 73-71 lead before the Suns came back. Booker's four-point play with 35 seconds left in the third quarter made it 99-89 for Phoenix. Luke Kennard's 3-pointer pushed the Suns' lead to 117-102 with 6:07 remaining in the game. Kennard had 11 points and three 3-pointers in his Suns debut after missing the season opener with a knee injury. The Warriors made 17 of 39 3-pointers (43.6%) and turned 19 offensive rebounds into 26 points. The Suns knocked the Warriors out of the postseason a year ago with a 111-96 victory in the play-in round. Lendeborg had six points on a pair of threes and Graham Ike had six points and five rebounds in the first quarter, when the Warriors took an early seven-point lead and had a 25-22 edge at the quarter. Ike, a 6-foot-9 rookie, made his second straight start at center as the Warriors also played without Kristaps Porzingis, who is not with the team because of an undisclosed health issue. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kirill Kaprizov's early goal sets tone as Wild handle Kraken
item.description: Kirill Kaprizov scored his NHL-leading 12th goal of the season and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the host Seattle Kraken 5-1 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kirill Kaprizov scored his NHL-leading 12th goal of the season and added an assist as the Minnesota Wild defeated the host Seattle Kraken 5-1 on Saturday night. Blake Coleman scored twice, including an empty-netter with 3:36 remaining, while Joel Eriksson Ek added a goal and an assist and Olli Maatta also tallied for the Wild. Minnesota snapped a two-game losing streak and improved to 1-1-1 on its five-game trip, which concludes with stops Sunday at Vancouver and Tuesday at Utah. Goaltender Jesper Wallstedt made 23 saves. Berkly Catton scored for Seattle, which had won its previous two games. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 shots. Kaprizov, who is tied for first in goals with the Edmonton Oilers' Leon Draisaitl, opened the scoring on a breakaway just 26 seconds into the game. He skated down the left wing before cutting across the low slot and putting a backhander over a sprawling Daccord. Seattle tied the score at 10:13 as Catton lifted a sharp-angled shot from low on the right wing just over Wallstedt's shoulder and inside the near post. The goal came one second after a power play expired. The Wild pulled away with three unanswered goals in the second period. Coleman scored on a breakaway at 2:11 just after he exited the penalty box, beating Daccord with a snap shot low to the glove side. Maatta made it 3-1 at 11:33 with a wrist shot from the left point that found the far upper corner of the net past a screened Daccord. Eriksson Ek added another at 13:00, after Daccord made a save on Matt Boldy's shot from the top of the left faceoff circle. The goalie couldn't quite corral the rebound and Eriksson Ek chipped the puck over Daccord's right shoulder. Kraken forward Jared McCann, the franchise's career scoring leader, didn't play as team officials said he's still being evaluated for a lower-body injury sustained in a 5-3 victory Thursday against Utah. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eleven shot near Florida A&M university in Tallahassee
item.description: A shooting near a Florida university campus in Tallahassee on Saturday night left 11 people with gunshot wounds and another injured, authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A shooting near a Florida university campus in Tallahassee on Saturday night left 11 people with gunshot wounds and another injured, authorities said. The shooting took place near Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University's campus on Perry Street, the university said, while police counted six adults and six juveniles among the injured. "At least three of the shooting victims have sustained serious injuries, while nine others are reported to be in stable condition," the Tallahassee police said in a statement. Initial findings showed a "physical altercation" preceded the shooting, police said, without elaborating. "It is especially heartbreaking to know that children are among those injured," said police chief Lawrence Revell. The youngest of those shot was 11, the NY Post newspaper said, but police did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. An altercation at a homecoming party escalated into gunfire and a fight between two or three individuals led to shots being fired just before 8 p.m., the paper added. Police said their violent crimes unit was investigating the circumstances. "The safety and security of our students, faculty, and staff remain our highest priority," Florida A&M said on X.

item.title: Dmitri Simashev’s first 2 career goals help Mammoth beat Lightning in OT
item.description: Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting the Utah Mammoth to a 5-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday night in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dmitri Simashev scored his first NHL goal and also netted the game-winning tally in overtime, lifting the Utah Mammoth to a 5-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday night in Salt Lake City. After Tampa Bay defenseman J.J. Moser and Utah blue-liner Nate Schmidt were stopped on breakaways in the opening 68 seconds of extra time, Simashev -- also on the rear guard -- slipped in a pass from Barrett Hayton at 1:44 for his first career game-winner. Utah also received goals from Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther and Anders Lee. Vincent Trocheck had two assists. Mammoth goaltender Karel Vejmelka made 29 saves and earned the secondary assist on Simashev's winner. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg, Brayden Point and Conor Geekie hit the net for Tampa Bay. In the second half of a back-to-back, goalie Dennis Hildeby made 23 saves for the Lightning, who played without captain Victor Hedman. Nikita Kucherov collected an assist for his 1,138th career point, passing Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead. In the opening period, Guentzel was credited with his seventh goal on a shot into traffic at 5:10 that Utah defenseman Mikhail Sergachev inadvertently put in past Vejmelka. Yamamoto knotted it less than two minutes later when he streaked out and sent a puck in on an odd-man rush. The shot clicked off Hildeby's stick for Yamamoto's third tally. However, Holmberg answered with his third marker a little over three minutes later. In a milestone moment, Kucherov dished out the primary assist to Point on the Lightning's second power play for a 3-1 lead. The historic point prompted the entire visiting bench of players to empty onto the ice and surround the Hart Trophy winner in celebration. The Mammoth also scored on their second power play, as Guenther ripped in his fifth marker to leave the first period trailing 3-2. Vejmelka stopped Point on a breakaway at 1:54 of the second period, but Geekie netted at 5:32 for a 4-2 lead that appeared to put the visitors in full control. However, the Central Division-leading Mammoth rallied behind Lee's third tally and the first NHL goal for Simashev less than three minutes apart for a 4-all tie through 40 minutes ahead of a scoreless third period. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nuggets rally from 23 down to force overtime, beat Pelicans
item.description: Jamal Murray had 42 points, Nikola Jokic finished with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the host Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jamal Murray had 42 points, Nikola Jokic finished with 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and the host Denver Nuggets rallied from a 23-point deficit to beat the New Orleans Pelicans 141-135 in overtime on Saturday night. Jokic has 199 career regular-season triple-doubles, second to just-retired Russell Westbrook's 209. Trevon Brazile scored seven of his 17 points in overtime and hit a corner 3-pointer late in the extra period, Christian Braun had 15 points in the game and DeMar DeRozan added 12 points for Denver. Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points, Dejounte Murray had 22, Zion Williamson and Derik Queen contributed 17 each, Saddiq Bey scored 14 and Jeremiah Fears added 10. New Orleans led 124-116 with 1:37 left in the fourth quarter before Jokic and Murray hit 3-pointers and Aaron Gordon's dunk made it a two-point game. Murray tied the game at 126 when he was fouled on a 3-point attempt and made 2 of 3 free throws with 16.8 seconds left, sending the game to overtime. Jokic's two free throws in the first minute of overtime gave the Nuggets their first lead since the first quarter. His turnaround jumper in the lane made it 130-128. After Bey split a pair of free throws, Brazile drained a 3-pointer for a 133-129 advantage, and Denver closed it out. The Pelicans raced to a 53-30 lead midway through the second quarter, but the Nuggets rallied in the final six minutes to get within 71-57 before Williamson's dunk in the final second made it a 16-point game at half. New Orleans' lead was 19 heading into the fourth, but the Nuggets rallied. With Murray and Jokic on the bench, Denver cut the deficit to 112-101 on Brazile's 3-pointer with 9:04 left, prompting a New Orleans timeout. The Pelicans extended the lead to 16 points at 118-102, but a 9-0 Nuggets run capped by Brazile's putback dunk made it 118-111. The Nuggets played without Julian Strawther (knee sprain), Spencer Jones (hamstring), Cameron Johnson (sprained ankle) and rookie Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist). New Orleans was without center Yves Missi after he suffered a knee bruise in a loss at Utah on Friday night. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brewers erase 4-run deficit, take 2-0 World Series lead vs. Rays
item.description: MILWAUKEE - Rookie Cooper Pratt made the most of his second opportunity.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE - Rookie Cooper Pratt made the most of his second opportunity. Pratt singled in the go-ahead run to atone for a costly error and the Milwaukee Brewers overcame a four-run deficit behind six scoreless innings from their lockdown bullpen for a 5-4 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday night and a 2-0 lead in the World Series. The Brewers, who trailed 4-0 in the first inning, took their first lead of Game 2 in the seventh when Brice Turang doubled to open off Tyler Wells (0-2) and advanced on a flyout. Pratt greeted Kevin Kelly with an RBI single to right to put Milwaukee up 5-4. "I need to be better defensively, but it's always awesome when you have an opportunity to kind of redeem yourself and make up for it," said the 22-year-old Pratt, inserted into the starting lineup after being called up from Triple-A Nashville in mid-June. "Probably wasn't the best swing, but it did the job and gave us the opportunity to score a run. I'm not going to complain." The Rays stranded the tying run at third in the ninth for the second consecutive game. Jonny DeLuca doubled to open the ninth off Aaron Ashby, who got the final two outs in the eighth. Victor Mesa Jr. struck out and DeLuca advanced to third on a groundout, but Yandy Diaz struck out swinging on a 3-2 count. "It's tough for teams to come in here and play. Our fans are so incredible. It's a tough environment to play in," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "Tampa Bay had us on the ropes every day. They had runners in scoring position when the game ended both days." Game 3 of the best-of-seven series is Monday in St. Petersburg, Fla. Only 10 teams have overcome a 2-0 deficit to win the World Series, the last being the New York Yankees in 1996. "These Milwaukee fans have been really loud. I know our fans are going to be really loud and excited to see us come back and kind of reset ourselves a little bit," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "We've got a really good pitcher going, as do they. A lot of confidence in this club to respond. They've done it all season long, and they'll continue to do it." Brewers starter Logan Henderson allowed four runs (three earned) on three hits in three innings, but the bullpen picked up its eighth win in nine postseason victories. The eight wins match the 2015 Kansas City Royals for most wins by relievers in a single postseason. JoJo Romero, Dustin May and DL Hall each followed Henderson with a scoreless inning. Abner Uribe (1-0) got four outs and Ashby finished for his third save. Ashby has not allowed a run in 15 2/3 innings over eight postseason appearances. "Our bullpen doesn't get enough credit," Murphy said. "I guess it does get a lot of credit, but you can't say enough great things about them. Six innings of shutout (work) again." Sal Frelick tied it at 4-all with a leadoff homer in the sixth off Ian Seymour. Frelick, who had four homers in 339 at-bats during the regular season, lined a 3-2 fastball 408 feet to center for his second career postseason homer. Milwaukee cut its 4-0 deficit in half with two runs in the bottom of the first, then capitalized on an error to pull within 4-3 in the fourth. Milwaukee threatened in the eighth, but Jackson Chourio was retired home trying to score from third on an infield bouncer on a close play that was upheld upon review. The Brewers, whose only other World Series appearance was as the American League representative in a seven-game loss to St. Louis in 1982, also overcame a 4-0 deficit in the NLCS, rallying for a 6-4 victory over the Dodgers in Game 4 to complete the sweep. Pratt's game-opening error contributed to the Rays' four-run first. Diaz continued to second on Pratt's errant throw from short, then scored on Chandler Simpson's one-out single. Simpson stole second and scored on Junior Caminero's RBI single. Liam Hicks followed with his first postseason homer to put the Rays up 4-0. The Brewers bunched four singles for two runs in the bottom half, including RBI singles by William Contreras and Garrett Mitchell. Milwaukee pulled within 4-3 in the fourth. Pratt battled back from an 0-2 count to draw a one-out walk, advanced to third on Frelick's single and scored on first baseman Jonathan Aranda's fielding error. Chourio prevented a run when his perfect throw home from left field nailed Hicks trying to score from second to end the sixth. That play was also upheld after a review. Rays starter Drew Rasmussen, who was 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA in three previous starts this postseason, allowed three runs on six hits in 3 2/3 innings. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Elections législatives en Serbie, l'opposition tente de renverser Vucic
item.description: Les Serbes se rendent aux urnes dimanche alors que les opposants du dirigeant populiste Aleksandar Vucic, qui a accédé au pouvoir en 2014, l'accusent de corruption.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les Serbes se rendent aux urnes dimanche alors que les opposants du dirigeant populiste Aleksandar Vucic, qui a accédé au pouvoir en 2014, l'accusent de corruption. Aleksandar Vucic a démissionné de ses fonctions de président le mois dernier après avoir annoncé la tenue d'élections anticipées, dans une tentative visant à prolonger son emprise sur le pouvoir en se présentant à nouveau au poste de Premier ministre. Les bureaux de vote ouvriront à 07h00 et fermeront à 20h00 (19h00 GMT). Les premiers résultats sont attendus environ deux heures plus tard. Aleksandar Vucic a été confronté à des manifestations anti-corruption déclenchées par l'effondrement, en novembre 2024, du toit de la gare de la ville de Novi Sad, dans le nord du pays, qui a tué 16 personnes. Une victoire de l'opposition estudiantine constituerait un profond bouleversement politique dans ce pays des Balkans comptant quelque 6 millions d'habitants. Elle pourrait également servir de modèle à d'autres mouvements étudiants à travers l'Europe, qui sont descendus dans la rue ces dernières semaines pour protester, parfois violemment, contre la mauvaise qualité de l'enseignement et le manque de perspectives d'avenir. Depuis son accession au pouvoir en 2014, Aleksandar Vucic a supervisé une période de développement économique mais a également dû faire face à un mécontentement croissant face à ce que ses opposants qualifient de corruption et d'autoritarisme. Il bénéficie toutefois du soutien de sa formation, le Parti progressiste serbe, qui l'a désigné comme candidat au poste de Premier ministre.

item.title: Kevin Durant leads balanced attack as Rockets take down Hawks
item.description: Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as the visiting Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-114 on Saturday to improve to 3-0.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kevin Durant led seven double-figure scorers with 22 points as the visiting Houston Rockets beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-114 on Saturday to improve to 3-0. The last time Houston opened a season with three straight wins was in 2017-18, when the Rockets went on to post a franchise-record 65 victories and reach the Western Conference finals. Houston extended its winning streak against Atlanta to five games. The teams will meet again Monday in Houston. The Rockets held the high-scoring Hawks, who averaged 130 points while winning their first two games, to a season-low point total. Houston also got 19 points apiece from Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard, who started in place of Fred VanVleet (right knee load management). Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each scored 17 points, with Sengun grabbing 10 rebounds and Thompson collecting 11. Atlanta was led by Jalen Johnson, who fell just shy of a triple-double with 26 points, 16 assists and nine rebounds. Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels scored 18 points apiece, and CJ McCollum added 17. The Rockets capitalized on Atlanta's struggles from beyond the arc. The Hawks made just 5 of 22 3-point attempts in the first half, including 1 of 10 in the second quarter, and finished 13 of 49 (26.5%) from deep. Houston shot 40% (14 of 35) from 3-point range. The Rockets led by as many as 20 points at 108-88 in the fourth quarter, but Atlanta mounted a late rally with a 9-0 run and cut the deficit to five with 37 seconds remaining. Durant sealed the win with two free throws with 19 seconds left. Atlanta scored the game's first seven points, but Houston responded with a 10-1 run to take a 10-8 lead. The Rockets led 30-26 after the first quarter, fueled by 10 points from Atlanta-area native Jabari Smith Jr. Houston continued to build its advantage, leading by as many as 11 points before taking a 59-48 lead into halftime. The game's start time was pushed back 30 minutes to accommodate the Atlanta Dream's WNBA Finals game Saturday afternoon. The later tipoff did not appear to affect Houston, which did not arrive in Atlanta until after 5 a.m. local time. --Field Level Media

item.title: Portuguese police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, make arrests
item.description: Portuguese police cleared a housing protest camp from the centre of Lisbon in the early hours of Sunday, charging demonstrators and making several arrests, with minor injuries reported, though figures were not immediately available.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Portuguese police cleared a housing protest camp from the centre of Lisbon in the early hours of Sunday, charging demonstrators and making several arrests, with minor injuries reported, though figures were not immediately available. Portugal is grappling with one of Europe's most acute home affordability crises, as prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, with young people among the hardest hit. "We have an obligation to fight for what we believe in," said one marcher, Vitor Gomes, 21, a multimedia communications student, adding that housing speculation, wealth concentration and rising inequality made him pessimistic about the future. Shortly after 2 a.m., dozens of officers, some with police dogs, moved in on the camp in Rossio Square, after warning protesters to remove their tents or face their dismantling, and threatening disobedience charges for those who resisted. Protesters had pitched more than 100 tents after Saturday's protest march by thousands along one of the capital's main avenues. Hundreds gathered to protect the encampment after police dismantled a similar camp there on Tuesday. The police action was "completely disproportionate", however, as there had been no public disorder, Left Bloc lawmaker Fabian Figueiredo said before the action. "The worst thing that could happen tonight was having this police force charge hundreds of people who are here peacefully. Why?" asked Figueiredo, who was at the camp. Protesters say soaring rents and higher living costs are squeezing households and turning housing into a growing source of discontent, with young people among those hardest hit. The Bank of Portugal estimates a shortfall of 300,000 homes nationwide, equivalent to Lisbon's entire housing stock. The protesters are demanding that the government scrap a [USN:L6N45M1AX TEXT:"bill"] to make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases, which passed a first parliamentary reading, although the far-right Chega party abstained. The protest followed similar demonstrations in Belgium, France, Italy and Spain.

item.title: Trae Young, Wizards hold off Bulls after dominant third quarter
item.description: Trae Young paired 25 points with nine assists and Kyshawn George added 22 points and nine rebounds as the Washington Wizards topped the host Chicago Bulls 124-120 on Saturday to open a three-game road trip.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Trae Young paired 25 points with nine assists and Kyshawn George added 22 points and nine rebounds as the Washington Wizards topped the host Chicago Bulls 124-120 on Saturday to open a three-game road trip. Washington outscored Chicago 40-20 in the third quarter to create separation and led by as many as 21 points down the stretch. Matas Buzelis swished a baseline three for the Bulls to cap a 16-4 run that cut the deficit to three points with 23.3 seconds to go. But Anthony Davis and Young combined to go 6-for-6 from the free-throw line the rest of the way to seal the result. The Wizards connected on 65.2% of their shots (15 of 23) in the third. Davis and George contributed nine points apiece in the quarter, with Young adding seven. Davis (19 points) and Tre Johnson (13) also scored in double figures for Washington, while Justin Champagnie had an 11-point, 14-rebound double-double. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson contributed 30 points and 14 rebounds for his first career double-double. Wilson, the fourth overall selection in the NBA Draft in June, scored 17 points in the first half to help Chicago to a 62-57 lead at the intermission. Wilson showed his athleticism and explosiveness with five first-half dunks. Wilson notched a pair of slams over a 1:07 span late in the second quarter, scoring off a long transition pass from Buddy Hield and on a reverse dunk off a putback. Chicago struggled to find balance and rhythm from the floor in the third quarter while Washington soared. The Bulls shot 30.4% (7 of 23) in the third quarter. A Norman Powell layup put Chicago ahead by three points at the 10:39 mark of the third, but Young tied the game with a trey on the next Washington possession. George's putback layup with 9:50 to go in the quarter gave the Wizards a lead they never relinquished. Buzelis scored 21 points for the Bulls. Powell added 18, Jalen Smith had 14 and Tre Jones 10. Josh Giddey had nine points, 10 assists and eight rebounds. The Bulls sputtered from 3-point range, shooting 27.9% (12 of 43). Washington wasn't much better from distance, making 10 of 33 (30.3%). AJ Dybantsa of Washington, the No. 1 overall selection in the draft, remained out with a sprained left ankle. The win helped the Wizards stop a five-game losing streak against the Bulls. --Field Level Media

item.title: British PM Burnham open to adopting EU free movement, Sunday Times reports
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the door to the country readopting the European Union’s free-movement rules, the Sunday Times reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the door to the country readopting the European Union’s free-movement rules, the Sunday Times reported on Saturday. In an interview with the newspaper, Burnham said the nature of immigration into Britain had been “different” since Brexit, with more foreigners moving permanently rather than returning to their home countries. “I think you have to have a very factual, quite evidence-based debate about this,” he said, making clear that staying out of free movement would not be a red line for talks, the newspaper added.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama, Spurs pull away from short-handed Mavs
item.description: Victor Wembanyama scored 23 points as the visiting San Antonio Spurs earned their first win of the season Saturday by defeating the short-handed Dallas Mavericks 122-106 in the second of a back-to-back for both teams.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Victor Wembanyama scored 23 points as the visiting San Antonio Spurs earned their first win of the season Saturday by defeating the short-handed Dallas Mavericks 122-106 in the second of a back-to-back for both teams. The Mavericks played without stars Cooper Flagg (shoulder) and Kyrie Irving, who was held out for left knee injury management. Flagg sprained his left shoulder in a win at Indiana on Friday and will be reevaluated next week. The Spurs led 77-63 four minutes into the third quarter but the Mavs cut their deficit to three heading to the final period. San Antonio opened the fourth quarter with a 11-3 run that produced a 103-92 edge at the 9:05 mark. From there, it was all Spurs. San Antonio led by 23 down the stretch as the Mavericks ran out of gas. Dylan Harper added 22 points, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle scored 19 each, Julian Champagnie hit for 12 off the bench and Devin Vassell tallied 11 points for San Antonio, which shot 47.5% from the field. Wembanyama also posted seven rebounds and four blocks. Rookie Sergio De Larrea's 21 points led Dallas. Marcus Sasser, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford scored 12 apiece, Zaccharie Risacher had 11 and Naji Marshall contributed 10 as the Mavericks shot 51.1% from the field. Washington's dunk after a Risacher steal with 38 seconds left in the first quarter put Dallas ahead by one. The Spurs' Carter Bryant answered with a dunk to grant San Antonio a 32-31 lead after 12 minutes of play. The Mavericks went up by six after a mid-second-quarter surge capped by Sasser's pullup jumper with 5:23 to play. San Antonio swung back, forging a 14-3 run punctuated by Keldon Johnson's tip-in layup at the 2:08 mark for a 59-54 advantage. San Antonio led 68-60 at the break behind Fox's 15 points, 12 from Wembanyama and 11 by Castle. De Larrea paced the Mavericks with 13 points off the bench, with Washington and Marshall adding 10 each. The Spurs expanded their lead to 14 early in the third before Dallas roared back, scoring 22 of the ensuing 29 points and regaining the lead at 85-84. The game went to the fourth quarter with San Antonio up 92-89 as Castle and Wembanyama hit late threes. --Field Level Media

item.title: ATP roundup: Taylor Fritz to face Lorenzo Musetti in Lyon title match
item.description: Second-seeded Taylor Fritz drilled 15 aces while overwhelming fellow American Tommy Paul 6-3, 7-5 on Saturday to reach the final at the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes in Lyon, France.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Second-seeded Taylor Fritz drilled 15 aces while overwhelming fellow American Tommy Paul 6-3, 7-5 on Saturday to reach the final at the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes in Lyon, France. Fritz also saved all nine break points he faced during the strong semifinal performance against the fourth-seeded Paul. Fritz had a 32-26 edge in winners and both players committed 21 unforced errors. Fritz will next face sixth-seeded Lorenzo Musetti, who defeated fellow Italian and top seed Flavio Cobolli 4-6, 6-2, 7-5 in the other semifinal. Musetti saved four match points in the final set to hold off Cobolli. He committed just 22 unforced errors compared to 36 for Cobolli. Musetti will be chasing his third ATP title. He is 4-3 all-time against Fritz and has won four of the past five meetings. Fritz will be aiming for his 12th career ATP crown. BNP Paribas Fortis European Open Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff recorded 15 aces and outlasted top-seeded Arthur Fils of France 6-4, 6-7 (7), 7-6 (5) to reach the final in Brussels. Fils carded 17 aces and saved 7 of 10 break points but could not stop Struff, who won the final two points of the tiebreaker to win the match. Struff had a 43-42 edge in winners and won 18 of 27 points at the net. Struff next faces Dutchman Tallon Griekspoor, who rallied for a 2-6, 6-3, 7-6 (4) victory over No. 3 Francisco Cerundolo of Argentina. Griekspoor had a 9-3 edge in aces and committed 24 unforced errors, nine fewer than Cerundolo. Griekspoor has won all three previous meetings against Struff. He is looking for his fourth ATP title, while Struff is vying to win his second. Almaty Open Top-seeded Russian Daniil Medvedev advanced to his second straight Almaty Open final Saturday when third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan retired with a knee injury after losing the opening set 6-3. Defending champion Medvedev had a 9-3 edge in aces in the first set as Bublik struggled to move on the court. After the match, Bublik said he injured his knee in his quarterfinal win over Russian Karen Khachanov on Friday and was advised by doctors not to play shortly before the start of Saturday's match. Medvedev will now face Georgian qualifier Nikoloz Basilashvili, who defeated No. 7 Greek Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-3 in his semifinal. Basilashvili had a 35-19 edge in winners while Tsitsipas had an 11-7 advantage in aces. Medvedev won the lone meeting against Basilashvili, winning in the round of 32 in 2022 at Vienna. Medvedev is gunning for his 25th career ATP title while Basilashvili is looking for his sixth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cavaliers hold off Nets for first win of season
item.description: Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers built a 22-point lead before holding on for a 125-121 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points and Jarrett Allen had 21 points and eight rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers built a 22-point lead before holding on for a 125-121 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Saturday night. Evan Mobley added 20 points and 10 rebounds, and Jaylon Tyson scored 15 points off the bench in Cleveland's home opener. James Harden collected 12 points, eight rebounds and seven assists as the Cavaliers picked up their first win. Brooklyn, which trailed 104-82 with 9:29 remaining, pulled within 123-121 on Michael Porter Jr.'s 3-pointer with 8.1 seconds left. Porter fouled out on the subsequent possession and Sam Merrill made two free throws for the Cavaliers to put them up four points with 5.2 seconds remaining. Porter finished with 28 points and nine rebounds, Julius Randle had 23 points and Egor Demin scored 15 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter for winless Brooklyn. Demin made four 3-pointers in the fourth and had six assists in the game. Peyton Watson had 11 points in his home debut for the Cavaliers, who squandered a 29-point lead Thursday and lost 114-106 to LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers. Chaney Johnson chipped in 10 points for the Nets. Day'Ron Sharpe posted seven points, eight rebounds and six personal fouls before being ejected after two flagrant fouls -- both on Harden 3-point tries -- to earn an automatic ejection. Demin and Watson also fouled out. The Cavaliers took the largest lead of the first half at 68-54 on a Watson layup heading into the break. Mobley, Allen and Porter each scored 13 points in the first half, and Harden had seven points, six rebounds and five assists. Mario Hezonja buried a 3-pointer as time expired in the first quarter, pushing Cleveland's advantage to 35-30. Mobley and Allen had eight points apiece, while Porter paced the Nets with seven points and four rebounds. Mitchell was struck on the head by Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. in the first quarter, briefly delaying the game while he lay under the basket. Brown, who is on a minutes restriction indefinitely because of a left ankle injury, will not play Sunday at home against the Indiana Pacers. The sixth overall pick "is on a long-term plan to build him up properly (physically)," according to coach Jordi Fernandez. Brooklyn was coming off a 110-103 home loss to the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday. Randle and Porter combined for 59 points and were the only Nets in double figures in that game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rosario Central gana a Huracán y lidera la tabla anual argentina
item.description: Rosario Central se puso en lo más alto de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino tras vencer el sábado 2-0 como local a Huracán en la decimocuarta jornadas del Torneo Clausura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rosario Central se puso en lo más alto de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino tras vencer el sábado 2-0 como local a Huracán en la decimocuarta jornadas del Torneo Clausura. Con el triunfo, el equipo llegó a 56 puntos en la tabla general y superó en dos unidades a Boca Juniors y Argentinos Juniors. “Estamos en un momento alegre y se ve dentro de la cancha la buena energía. La idea es pelear, nos están saliendo muy bien las cosas y vamos por todo”, dijo el colombiano Jáminton Campaz a la televisión local. En el Gigante de Arroyito, el local abrió el marcador a los 20 minutos con un cabezazo de Emanuel Coronel tras un centro de Campaz. Ángel Di María marcó el segundo a los 84 minutos, tras una asistencia de Franco Ibarra. Por su parte, San Lorenzo empató sin goles como local ante Newell’s Old Boys y quedó noveno en su zona, fuera de los puestos de clasificación a la postemporada, a dos fechas del final de la fase regular. “El equipo hizo un partido correcto. Tuvimos orden. Lo que nos faltó para ganar fue presencia en el área. Quedan dos finales por delante”, dijo el entrenador de San Lorenzo, Rubén Insua, en conferencia de prensa. En otros partidos del sábado, Defensa y Justicia venció 2-1 a Talleres de Córdoba y Banfield y Lanús igualaron 1-1. El viernes, Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata derrotó 2-0 a Sarmiento, Platense venció 2-1 a Gimnasia de Mendoza y Atlético Tucumán ganó 1-0 a Tigre.
