item.title: Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms
item.description: US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that. Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied to White House renovations. Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Campaigning in Michigan for US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Obama framed the November 3 vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency. "We got to flip that circuit breaker, bring some accountability to this government," Obama said. Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats. They hope that bringing him into the race can fire up their supporters for a tight US Senate race in which El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former US representative. The former president obliged the Michigan crowd by playing to Democrats' frequently repeated criticisms of Trump and of Republicans' willingness to go along with him. "We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, on your dime, like this," Obama said. "Never seen a president so intent on selling favors like this ... Now the party seems to stand for corrupt government, or inept government, or no government." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A Reuters/Ipsos poll in August found that 63% of Americans think the president and his family have [USN:L6N44F13X TEXT:"inappropriately profited"] from cryptocurrency since he returned to the White House last year and that 69% believe his policy decisions are influenced by his private business dealings. Obama also ridiculed the administration's claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters. "Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, where oil goes through to get to the world," Obama said. The former president also accused the Trump administration of emphasizing unimportant matters, sarcastically calling Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth someone "laser-focused on important matters like the jawline and testosterone levels of our troops" and ridiculing White House renovations as tacky. "He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory," Obama said.

item.title: Joel Embiid posts triple-double, 76ers handle Bucks
item.description: Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 127-116 home win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joel Embiid recorded his 10th career triple-double and Jaylen Brown scored 27 points on his 30th birthday to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 127-116 home win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Embiid finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for Philadelphia, which rested LeBron James (back/sciatica). James is expected to play Sunday against the Detroit Pistons, while Embiid will rest in the second half of a back-to-back. Tyrese Maxey pitched in with 26 points for the Sixers, while VJ Edgecombe made five 3-pointers as part of a 17-point, 13-rebound performance. While the Sixers are 3-0 on the young season, the Bucks fell to 0-3 despite eight players scoring in double figures. Jaime Jaquez Jr. led Milwaukee with 21 points, while Kel'el Ware had 19 points and 13 rebounds off the bench for the visitors. The teams were tied at 82-82 with four minutes left in the third quarter before the Sixers ended the period on a 15-5 push. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Maxey each made a 3-pointer during that surge, which Maxey capped with a tough fadeaway with the quarter winding down. Philadelphia started to pull away early in the fourth. Embiid's jumper gave the hosts a 113-98 lead with six minutes left. The Sixers still held a comfortable advantage at 117-108 with 3:18 to go before the Bucks rattled off six in a row in just over a minute to make it a three-point game. However, Edgecombe came up with a big offensive rebound on the other end, leading to a 3-pointer by Brown. Then on the next Philadelphia possession, Brown found Caldwell-Pope for a 3-pointer that essentially sealed the outcome. Philadelphia knocked down five 3-pointers in the first quarter -- three by Edgecombe -- en route to a 34-25 lead after 12 minutes. The Sixers struggled to find a rhythm in the second quarter, as they shot just 33.3% from the field (9 of 27). Brown led all scorers with 16 points in the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Adam Fantilli nets OT winner, Blue Jackets edge Golden Knights
item.description: Adam Fantilli scored a power-play goal 59 seconds into overtime to lead the Columbus Blue Jackets to a 2-1 victory over the visiting Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Adam Fantilli scored a power-play goal 59 seconds into overtime to lead the Columbus Blue Jackets to a 2-1 victory over the visiting Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday night. With defenseman Shea Theodore in the penalty box for a holding penalty on Matthew Knies, Fantilli blasted a sharp-angled one-timer from the bottom of the right circle off a Charlie Coyle pass inside the near post and past the left shoulder of Vegas goaltender Carter Hart for the game-winner. It was Fantilli's third goal of the season and snapped a 0-for-22 drought on the power play for the Blue Jackets. It also marked the fifth straight game that the Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal in a contest. Denton Mateychuk also scored a goal and Kent Johnson added two assists for Columbus, which snapped a two-game losing streak and won for just the second time in six games. Cam Talbot finished with 26 saves. Tomas Hertl scored a goal for Vegas and Hart stopped 18 of 20 shots for Vegas, which saw its losing streak extended to a season-high three games. Columbus took a 1-0 lead at the 11:51 mark of the first period when Mateychuk, cutting through the slot, took a pass from Johnson and put a backhander inside the right post for his second goal of the campaign. Vegas, coming off back-to-back 6-2 losses to Tampa Bay and at St. Louis, tied it near the end of the first period when Hertl roofed a rebound of a Braeden Bowman shot from the low slot for his fifth goal. Trevor Connelly was credited with a second assist. That would end the scoring in regulation with Hart and Talbot both making highlight-reel glove saves on close-in shots from near the right post to keep the game even. Hart gloved a shot by Sean Monahan while Talbot stopped Jack Eichel's try. Vegas outshot Columbus 13-5 in the third period, but could not dent the net. The Golden Knights, who had a three-game winning streak against Columbus snapped, played their second straight game without forward Mitch Marner, who remained in Las Vegas for the birth of his child. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ville Koivunen scores OT winner as Penguins rally past Predators
item.description: Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for the ailing Pittsburgh Penguins, who rallied to take down the visiting Nashville Predators 3-2 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ville Koivunen scored with 1:16 left in overtime for the ailing Pittsburgh Penguins, who rallied to take down the visiting Nashville Predators 3-2 on Saturday night. Connor Dewar and Rickard Rakell also scored for the Penguins, who won their second straight game. Arturs Silovs finished with 24 saves for Pittsburgh, marking the first time the team has won consecutive games since starting the season 2-0. Steven Stamkos scored his fifth of the season and Jayden Struble notched his first for the Predators, who are 0-4 in overtime and shootout games. Juuse Saros made a season-high 34 saves, but Rakell spoiled his bid for a victory by tying the game with 1:06 remaining in regulation. Pittsburgh played without Evgeni Malkin, who missed the game due to an illness. Malkin's longtime teammates, though, made sure the Penguins earned at least a point. With Silovs on the bench for an extra attacker, Sidney Crosby controlled the puck in the left faceoff circle. Instead of shooting, he fed Rakell at the other circle and Rakell buried it before Saros could glide across the crease. Saros had stopped Rakell twice on breakaways earlier in the game, including a short-handed chance with less than eight minutes left. Nashville coach Andrew Brunette moved Matthew Wood onto the top line alongside Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly following Thursday's 6-0 loss at Boston. The trio produced the game's opening goal at 9:24 of the first period when Wood's shot deflected off Stamkos' skate. Pittsburgh capitalized on a Predators turnover to draw even early in the second period. Adam Wilsby's failed clearance behind the net allowed Dewar to tie the game just 18 seconds into the period. It was one of 24 giveaways for Nashville. Struble, acquired from Montreal on Oct. 9 for a second-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft, restored Nashville's lead at 6:40 of the second period. Besides Malkin missing the game, Pittsburgh has six skaters on injured reserve. Egor Chinakhov also missed his second straight game due to a lower-body injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Drake Batherson (hat trick), Senators too strong for Rangers
item.description: Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as the Ottawa Senators topped the visiting New York Rangers 7-4 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Batherson scored a hat trick and added an assist as the Ottawa Senators topped the visiting New York Rangers 7-4 on Saturday night. Jake Sanderson tallied one goal and added two assists, while Dylan Cozens and Michael Amadio each scored and chipped in a helper for Ottawa. Tim Stutzle also found the back of the net as the Senators improved to 5-2-0 on home ice. Jonas Johansson, making his Senators and season debut, made 24 saves. J.T. Miller and Will Cuylle each scored and added an assist, and Alexis Lafreniere and Pavel Dorofeyev also scored for the Rangers, who are 1-3-1 in their last five. Adam Fox and Noah Laba each added a pair of helpers, and Dylan Garand stopped 17 shots for New York. Trailing 5-3, Dorofeyev got the Rangers to within one, one-timing a Cuylle feed past Johansson for his third goal this season at 15:32 of the third. Amadio scored into an empty net with 1:14 remaining for his third of the season. Batherson completed the hat trick with an empty-netter at 19:48 of the third. Sanderson gave the Senators a 5-3 lead at 13:38 of the third, backhanding the rebound off Ridly Greig's shot for his first of the season. Lafreniere pulled the Rangers to 4-3 with 26 seconds remaining in the second period, snapping home a 2-on-1 feed from Miller for his ninth of the season. Trailing 4-1, New York cut the lead in half as Miller batted home a bouncing puck for his third of the season at 12:54 of the second period. The Senators took a 4-1 lead at 11:21 as Batherson's centering pass directed off Cozens' skate and past Garand. Cuylle got the Rangers on the board, short-handed, at the midway mark of the second, snapping a Laba feed past Johansson. Batherson added his second of the night to give the Sens a 3-0 lead at 1:47 of the middle frame, putting home the rebound off Cozens' shot. The Senators jumped out to an early 2-0 lead, scoring twice in a 1:06 span of the first period. Ottawa opened the scoring at 5:33 of the first as Batherson snapped a Sanderson feed short-side past Garand. Stutzle doubled the Senators' lead at 6:39, tapping in a cross-ice feed from Fabian Zetterlund. --Field Level Media

item.title: Four-goal third propels surging Maple Leafs past Oilers
item.description: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: William Nylander scored two of Toronto's four third-period goals as the visiting Maple Leafs extended their winning streak to four with a 7-2 drubbing of the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday. Jack Roslovic recorded a goal and an assist, while Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored and Kirill Marchenko nabbed two assists. For Edmonton, Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard had two helpers each. Anthony Stolarz stopped 30 shots for his fourth victory as Toronto posted its first four-game win streak since January. Tristan Jarry turned away 25 shots for the Oilers, who had won three in a row. Roslovic received credit for Toronto's opening goal in a high-octane opening frame as both teams' injury-riddled blue lines struggled to contain their speedy opponents. Jarry made a pad save to deny Easton Cowan on a 2-on-1 before Roslovic batted the puck towards goal. Oilers defenseman Jake Walman inadvertently chipped the puck into his own net in a desperate attempt to clear it away 14:16 into the period. Roslovic sprung Cowan on another 2-on-1 early in the second period. Cowan played the puck through the legs of Ryan Shea and onto the tape of Matthews, who ripped it into the open cage 5:29 into the period. Fresh off his game-winning goal against the New York Rangers on Thursday, Stecher exchanged passes with Marchenko and fired it past Jarry from the high slot to make it 3-0. Draisaitl finally solved Stolarz during a period of 4-on-4 play, receiving a drop pass from McDavid and floating one through a maze of bodies to make it 3-1 with 56 seconds remaining in the second. Nylander restored Toronto's three-goal lead 14 seconds into its first power play and 5:59 into the third period off a powerful one-timer from the center of the faceoff circle. MacEwen scored his first goal as a Maple Leaf in a bizarre sequence, driving on net and batting in his rebound 13:39 into the period. Draisaitl scored on the power play three minutes later, then Nylander scored an empty-netter with 2:04 remaining. Lettieri followed with his first Toronto goal with 31 seconds left. --Field Level Media

item.title: Election présidentielle en Bulgarie dans un contexte d'attaques en mer Noire
item.description: Les Bulgares sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour une élection présidentielle qui intervient alors que la guerre en Ukraine s'étend au large de la côte bulgare en mer Noire.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les Bulgares sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour une élection présidentielle qui intervient alors que la guerre en Ukraine s'étend au large de la côte bulgare en mer Noire. Les sondages placent la présidente sortante Iliana Iotova, 61 ans, et l'ancien Premier ministre par intérim Andreï Giourov, 50 ans, en tête alors que 27 candidats s'opposent. Bien que la fonction présidentielle soit essentiellement honorifique en Bulgarie, le scrutin de dimanche revêt une importance accrue après une série d'attaques de drones contre des navires marchands en mer Noire, au large de la côte bulgare. Ces attaques, qui ont suscité une condamnation internationale et des inquiétudes quant à une extension de la guerre en Ukraine, ont poussé le gouvernement à solliciter l'aide de ses alliés pour renforcer la sécurité maritime. La Bulgarie s'est abstenue d'accuser directement Moscou d'être à l'origine de ces attaques, mais le Premier ministre Roumen Radev a déclaré que leurs conséquences "profitaient à la Fédération de Russie". Les deux principaux candidats à l'élection présidentielle ont condamné ces attaques, mais leurs positions divergent quant à la guerre dans son ensemble. Andreï Giourov bénéficie du soutien des partis réformistes pro-occidentaux et exprime depuis longtemps son soutien à l'Ukraine. Il a signé un accord de coopération en matière de sécurité avec Kyiv lorsqu'il occupait le poste de Premier ministre par intérim cette année. Iliana Iotova, ancienne vice-présidente, est devenue présidente par intérim en janvier après la démission de Roumen Radev, qui s'était déclaré candidat aux élections législatives, un scrutin qu'il a remporté grâce à un programme considéré par de nombreux analystes politiques comme favorable au Kremlin. Si Iliana Iotova remportait l'élection, elle deviendrait la première femme élue à la présidence en Bulgarie. Les bureaux de vote ouvriront à 07h00 (05h00 GMT) et fermeront à 20h00.

item.title: Bruins tally 4 in the 3rd to edge Sharks, extend unbeaten streak to 8
item.description: The Boston Bruins scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, to edge the visiting San Jose Sharks 6-4 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Boston Bruins scored four third-period goals, including three in a row to erase a 3-2 deficit, to edge the visiting San Jose Sharks 6-4 on Saturday night. David Pastrnak tied former teammate Patrice Bergeron for third on Boston's all-time goals list (427) to kick off the late-game surge. Fraser Minten (game-winner), James Hagens and Casey Mittelstadt all had a goal and an assist, while Marat Khusnutdinov and Will Borgen also lit the lamp for the Bruins, who are 7-0-1 in their last eight games. Boston's Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka each dished out two assists, and Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves. Michael Misa, Kiefer Sherwood, Dmitry Orlov and Will Smith each scored a goal, Jacob Trouba had two assists, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 shots for San Jose, which was on a two-game win streak. Orlov's one-time blast from the center point off an Ivar Stenberg pass gave San Jose its first lead of the night at 3-2 4:03 into the third, but two goals in 40 seconds put the Bruins back in front. Pastrnak jumped right out of the box from a tripping penalty and tied the game at 8:27, taking Peterka's feed into the top of the right circle and firing off a wrister past Nedeljkovic's blocker. Hagens gave Boston a 4-3 lead when he followed up Lindholm's chance in front at 9:07. With the Bruins on a four-minute power play, Minten added an insurance marker at 12:00, burying a rebound after Nedeljkovic robbed Peterka. San Jose would not go quietly. Smith made it a one-goal game again with a 4-on-4 goal with 7:33 left in regulation, slotting home Trouba's feed to the right circle after Macklin Celebrini circled the zone with the puck. With 30 seconds to go, Borgen finished into an empty net. Mittelstadt opened the scoring with his 100th career goal only 3:08 into the opening period, finishing off a relentless shift with Lindholm and Hagens by netting a loose puck from outside the right crease. San Jose's power play evened the score at 5:54. Tyler Toffoli's shot from above the right circle was deflected and found the stick of Misa, who slotted it into a virtually open net from the left side. Strong net-front play allowed the Bruins to jump back in front at 8:20 of the second. After Minten found Morgan Geekie between the circles, Khusnutdinov slipped in from the left side and buried a backhand high to Nedeljkovic's glove side. Swayman denied Sherwood's partial short-handed breakaway off a turnover earlier in the period, but could not stop a second as the Sharks made it 2-2 at 13:34. Sherwood broke up Lindholm's pass in the neutral zone and broke in ahead, putting home a top-shelf shot. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alex Tuch scores twice, lifts Capitals past former team Sabres in OT
item.description: Alex Tuch scored his second goal of the game at 3:42 of overtime Saturday to lift the host Washington Capitals to a 4-3 victory over his former team, the Buffalo Sabres.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alex Tuch scored his second goal of the game at 3:42 of overtime Saturday to lift the host Washington Capitals to a 4-3 victory over his former team, the Buffalo Sabres. Tuch, acquired by Washington in a sign-and-trade deal with Buffalo in June, was in the slot to take a pass from Dylan Strome behind the net and beat a screened Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen inside the left post. Strome also scored twice, and Charlie Lindgren made 18 saves for the Capitals. Jack Quinn, Josh Doan and Noah Ostlund scored for the Sabres. Luukkonen made 30 saves. Quinn opened the scoring at 6:27 of the first period, taking a pass from Olen Zellweger along the half wall, moving through the circle to the net and lifting it short side over Lindgren. Doan made it 2-0 at 10:36. Ryan McLeod intercepted the puck in the corner and quickly fed an uncovered Doan, who fired a snapshot that beat Lindgren blocker side. Tuch cut Buffalo's lead to 2-1 at 16:10 of the first period when his centering pass from the right corner deflected off former teammate Tage Thompson's stick and into the net. Strome pulled the hosts even early in the second period. Jakob Chychrun's point shot deflected off Kyrou's stick on the way to the net, landing in front where Strome collected it and backhanded it past Luukkonen at 2:59. He then gave the Capitals their first lead of the game at 17:24. With Ostlund on his back, Justin Sourdif maintained possession behind the net before feeding Strome for a quick shot from the doorstep to make it 3-2. Ostlund tied it 3-3 at 2:20 of the third period. Owen Power fed an open Ostlund at the bottom of the right circle, and Ostlund's centering feed went off Kyrou's skate in front. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alpine F1 team defends Colapinto after Clarkson comments
item.description: The Alpine Formula One team issued a statement in support of their driver after Jeremy Clarkson joked that he would give him a grid penalty just for being Argentine.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: The Alpine Formula One team issued a statement in support of driver Franco Colapinto on Saturday after TV celebrity Jeremy Clarkson joked that he would give him a grid penalty just for being Argentine. Clarkson, famed for presenting British motoring programmes "Top Gear" and Amazon's "The Grand Tour" as well as the farming hit "Clarkson's Farm," made his comments in an interview with Sky Sports television ahead of the US Grand Prix. Colapinto has a 10-place grid penalty for Sunday's race at the Circuit of the Americas as a result of power unit component changes. "Franco's got a grid penalty for being Argentinian," said Clarkson, a guest of Alpine in Austin. "Probably. Well, I'd give him one for that. "That's just because of what happened when we went there," he added. Clarkson went to Argentina's Patagonia with Top Gear in 2014 in a controversial episode that triggered protests after he drove a car with a registration number that some saw as a reference to the 1982 war over the Falkland Islands that Argentina claims sovereignty over and knows as Las Malvinas. "We're aware of the comments made in a recent TV interview from a guest of the team in Austin," Renault-owned Alpine said, without mentioning Clarkson. "We would like to reiterate that these are personal views and do not align with the team's values of promoting kindness and respect. Franco is our driver and has our full support." Colapinto has a legion of Argentine fans and has had to repeatedly issue statements calling for restraint after rivals and even his own teammates received online abuse. The Argentine said in Austin earlier in the week that the bad comments had "crossed a few lines lately" and said his mechanics and engineers had been targeted by some supporters seeking blame for race incidents. "My mechanics got a lot of hate, my engineer, people from my team that want me to do well and help me perform," he said. "And I'm working with daily getting these kind of messages." Colapinto's manager Jamie Campbell-Walter posted on X that "Jeremy Clarkson’s comments about Franco’s nationality were completely unacceptable. There is no place for remarks like this in Formula One, regardless of who makes them or whether they are intended as a joke. "We have worked hard to promote respect and put an end to hostility and abuse. That respect must go both ways. We cannot ask anyone to behave responsibly while accepting comments like these from prominent figures visiting our sport."

item.title: Pyotr Kochetkov, Hurricanes blank Blues to finish road trip
item.description: Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves to lead the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes to a 4-0 road victory over the St. Louis Blues on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pyotr Kochetkov made 24 saves to lead the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes to a 4-0 road victory over the St. Louis Blues on Saturday. Sean Walker, Jesperi Kotkaniemi, Logan Stankoven, and Nikolaj Ehlers all lit the lamp as the Hurricanes closed out their five-game road trip with a victory. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis each picked up a pair of assists, while Joel Hofer finished with 35 saves in the losing effort. Connor McMichael picked off a pass and came down on a breakaway 1:30 into the middle frame, but Kochetkov shut down the opportunity with a glove save. The Hurricanes stormed down on an odd-man rush, but Hofer shut the door as he stopped Walker's shot and then Ehlers sent his rebound chance wide of the net just over four minutes into the second. Walker got his revenge less than a minute later as he took a pass from Jackson Blake and fired it past Hofer to tally the Hurricanes' first goal of the night on their 20th shot. Kotkaniemi swiftly doubled up their advantage as 20 seconds later he received a slick pass from Jordan Martinook and found the back of the net. Moments after the Blues failed to capitalize on their first power play of the contest, Jarvis sprung Stankoven on a breakaway and he fired it short side past Hofer to make it 3-0 with 6:25 left in the second. Kochetkov was tested early in the third, but once again he had the answer as he denied both Aleksanteri Kaskimaki and Dalibor Dvorsky under two minutes into the period. Ehlers made it 4-0 with 15:30 remaining in the third with a power-play marker. With the Blues' defenders scrambling around, Aho spotted Ehlers open and the Danish forward sent it into the empty cage for his fourth goal of the season. Stankoven had a chance to bury his second of the night off a turnover, but Hofer stoned him with the glove with 12:33 left in the third period. Each team was assessed only one minor penalty in the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Broncos activate LB Jonathon Cooper (arrest) from exempt list
item.description: The Denver Broncos activated edge rusher Jonathon Cooper ahead of Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Denver Broncos activated edge rusher Jonathon Cooper ahead of Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals. Cooper, 28, spent the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner's exempt list. During the offseason, he was arrested twice in June. He faces multiple charges, including felony second-degree assault by strangulation, and is set to stand trial in March. Cooper posted 27 total sacks over the last three seasons with the Broncos, including eight sacks in 2025. He also posted 50 combined tackles and four passes defended last season. Without Cooper, the Broncos' pass rush has still been very effective; Denver (4-2) is tied for fourth in the NFL in sacks (18). Zach Allen is leading the way with 4.5 sacks, while Nik Bonitto is not far behind at 3.5 sacks. Denver also activated running back Jonah Coleman and, in corresponding moves, placed running back Tyler Badie and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss on injured reserve. The Broncos also elevated safety Taylor Rapp and defensive back Sean Fresch Jr. from the practice squad to the active roster. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brésil-Lula et Bolsonaro mobilisent leurs partisans à la veille du second tour de la présidentielle
item.description: Le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro ont clôturé samedi leur campagne en vue du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, en mobilisant leurs partisans et en lançant un dernier appel aux électeurs indécis.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso, Sebastian Rocandio, Lais Morais
item.content:encoded: Le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro ont clôturé samedi leur campagne en vue du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, en mobilisant leurs partisans et en lançant un dernier appel aux électeurs indécis. En amont du scrutin de dimanche, les deux candidats sont au coude à coude dans les sondages, après que le sénateur de droite a remporté le premier tour du scrutin au début du mois. Un sondage CNT/MDA donnait au fils de l'ancien dirigeant d'extrême droite Jair Bolsonaro une avance de 1,3 point sur son adversaire. Lula, qui brigue un quatrième mandat non consécutif, a entamé sa dernière journée de campagne par une marche le long de la plage de Copacabana à Rio de Janeiro. "Nous allons remporter l'élection pour une raison simple: il est vrai que le peuple veut du changement, (mais) il veut aller de l'avant. Il ne veut pas revenir en arrière", a déclaré Lula aux journalistes avant le rassemblement. Plus tard, le président sortant a mené une autre marche à São Paulo. "C'est tellement enthousiasmant de voir tout le monde ici. C'est le genre d'énergie dont nous avons besoin pour le Brésil. Le Brésil est à nous", a déclaré Gisele Passos, une femme d'affaires de 61 ans présente au rassemblement de São Paulo. BOLSONARO FAIT CAMPAGNE DANS UN ETAT CLÉ Flavio Bolsonaro, quant à lui, s'est joint à un cortège de motos à Belo Horizonte, la capitale du Minas Gerais, un Etat clé de la campagne électorale. Aucun candidat n'a remporté une élection présidentielle sans s'imposer dans le Minas Gerais depuis les années 1980. Flavio Bolsonaro devançait Lula d'environ 5 points de pourcentage dans cet Etat lors du premier tour de scrutin. "Le moment est presque venu. Il ne reste que quelques heures avant que nous ne façonnions l'avenir de notre nation pour les 30 ou 40 prochaines années", a-t-il dit dans une vidéo publiée sur les réseaux sociaux. Flavio Bolsonaro a ensuite participé à un défilé dans son l'Etat de Rio de Janeiro, dont il est originaire et qu'il représente au Sénat depuis 2019.

item.title: Serbia votes in historic election as students seek to end Vucic's long grip on power
item.description: Serbia is voting on Sunday as a mass student protest movement seeks to unseat longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Ivana Sekularac, Edward Mcallister
item.content:encoded: Serbia is voting on Sunday as a mass student protest movement seeks to unseat longtime populist leader Aleksandar Vucic in the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade. The snap parliamentary elections, called by Vucic in September, come after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024. The students have since [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"gained widespread support"]. Early turnout was strong, with long lines forming in front of polling stations even before they opened at 7 a.m.. First indications of results are expected around two hours after polls close at 8 p.m. (1900 GMT). A student victory would be a profound political shift in the Balkan country of some 6 million people, reminiscent of the [USN:L1N40V01B TEXT:"defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban"] in April. It also potentially offers a blueprint for other student movements across Europe, which have [USN:L6N464038 TEXT:"taken to the streets"] in recent weeks to protest, [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"in some cases violently"], against poor education standards and a lack of prospects. "I came out early today because the students called us," said Ana, 30, at a polling station in Belgrade. Vucic, who resigned from his second term as president to run again for prime minister, is a strong incumbent. Many voters thank him for pulling Serbia from economic obscurity and orchestrating a period of sustained modernisation including new highways, railways, schools and hospitals. OPINION POLLS PREDICT TIGHT RACE Domestically, Vucic has pledged higher pensions and public sector salaries, investment in state healthcare and subsidies for young couples. On the international stage, he has balanced closer ties with China, a major investor, and Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, while leaving the door open to joining the European Union despite a stalled campaign. "I voted for our children, our young people...our children deserve peace and work, only Vucic can bring that," said Hatidza, a Roma. The students' domestic agenda aims to root out graft and improve schooling, but they have been quieter on their international ambitions. Their list of 250 largely unknown candidates includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic. "I hope that today will pass in a democratic atmosphere, in peace, and that we will legitimately elect a new government in Serbia," Srdanovic said after casting his vote in Novi Sad, adding that the scenes suggested there would be a record voter turnout in the country's recent history. In Belgrade, Vucic was still in the line to vote, having waited patiently for more than an hour. Opinion polls predict a tight race. In an Ipsos poll published on Thursday, Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) is seen leading with 47% of votes versus 40% for the students. But other polls have put the students in the lead. STUDENT PROTESTS INCREASE PRESSURE ON VUCIC The student-led street protests sparked by the station disaster quickly became the biggest in a generation, calling for Vucic to step down. Rights groups and activists say [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"repression has worsened"] in the period since. "These are historical elections. For decades the people have been waiting for this time, something to bring hope that we can live freely and by the rules of democracy," said actress Jelena Stupljanin, 48, at a Belgrade polling station. Vucic and the SNS have repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents. He says the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students dismiss. "This has been one of the most difficult but the most emotional campaigns," Vucic told his supporters on Thursday. "We stood against those who wanted to destroy Serbia."

item.title: Brandon Miller scores 34 as Hornets hold off Heat
item.description: Brandon Miller pumped in 34 points and the Charlotte Hornets recovered to beat the visiting Miami Heat 115-110 after a huge lead was wiped out in the fourth quarter Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Miller pumped in 34 points and the Charlotte Hornets recovered to beat the visiting Miami Heat 115-110 after a huge lead was wiped out in the fourth quarter Saturday night. Dennis Schroder added 25 points, Naz Reid scored 23 and Grayson Allen contributed 20, including a crucial four-point play. Miller was the only one of Charlotte's top four scorers who played for the Hornets last season. Davion Mitchell's 22 points and 10 assists paced the Heat, who remained winless through three games despite erasing a 23-point deficit to tie the score at 100. Bam Adebayo's 20 points and eight rebounds gave Miami a lift, Pelle Larsson supplied 15 points, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson each had 14, and Bobby Portis scored 13. The Hornets looked headed for a comfortable win less than 24 hours after a 47-point home-opener loss to the Atlanta Hawks. Still, the Heat erased a 23-point lead with a stunning comeback in the first six minutes of the fourth quarter. Miami opened the fourth quarter with a 10-2 run to cut the lead to 98-85. That run extended to a 25-4 edge as the Heat pulled even at 100-100 with less than six minutes to play. Mitchell provided the final five points of that rally. The Heat never took the lead, however, and Allen converted a four-point play to give Charlotte a 108-104 advantage. Schroder added two free throws before Miami mounted one final push. Mitchell's 3-pointer trimmed the gap to 113-110 with 8.1 seconds left. Allen countered with a pair of free throws. The Heat made 23 of 25 free-throw attempts to help offset 43% shooting from the field. Miller finished 10-for-29 from the field and made 11 of 12 free throws. Reid sank five of Charlotte's 16 baskets from 3-point range and Allen finished with four. Charlotte led 66-58 at halftime, then cranked out a 30-17 edge in the third quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Zach Edey, Grizzlies look to stay unbeaten vs. winless Kings
item.description: Two big men off to fast starts on opposite ends of the floor go head-to-head Sunday night when Zach Edey and the Memphis Grizzlies visit Domantas Sabonis and the Sacramento Kings.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two big men off to fast starts on opposite ends of the floor go head-to-head Sunday night when Zach Edey and the Memphis Grizzlies visit Domantas Sabonis and the Sacramento Kings. Edey drew high praise from Golden State coach Steve Kerr after his 10 rebounds and two blocks contributed to Memphis' 111-108 road win over the Warriors on Friday. The 7-foot-3 center recorded a plus-25 plus/minus, equaling the fifth-best of his three-year NBA career. He also found time for eight points, three assists and a steal. "Give them credit -- they did a great job of defending us," Kerr told the media after watching the Grizzlies hold the Warriors to two points over the final 3:47, as the visitors rallied from a 106-94 deficit. Edey blocked a Stephen Curry 3-point attempt during the run. "I thought Zach, his defense down the stretch, was really good," Kerr continued. "(He made) things difficult for us." Edey had similar numbers -- six points, nine rebounds, two blocks and a plus-19 plus/minus, when the Grizzlies opened the season with a home win over the Utah Jazz on Wednesday. Having watched Golden State attempt to attack his big man in a variety of ways, Memphis coach Tuomas Iisalo came away impressed with how his 305-pounder handled every challenge. "He was on (Graham) Ike. He was on (Draymond) Green. He was on (Gary) Payton (II). I think he was on (Al) Horford," Iisalo noted to reporters after the game. "(He) found a way to impact the game against all of these guys. "He's incredibly athletic. He finds a way within the game to make winning plays." As the Grizzlies attempt to open 3-0 for the first time since 2017, Edey and Sabonis will meet for the third time. The Kings have won on both previous occasions, but Sabonis has been held to an average of just 11.5 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.0 assists. The Sacramento star has been significantly more productive in the Kings' first two games this season. He had 14 points, 18 rebounds and eight assists in an opening road loss to the Los Angeles Clippers, then posted the 69th triple-double of his 11-year career with 27 points, 19 rebounds and 10 assists when Sacramento dropped its home opener to the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday. Sabonis admitted after the game he'd gladly have traded some of his baskets for assists and looks forward to being more of a passer than a shooter in games ahead. "Move the ball," he expressed to the media. "Get me the ball more so I can swing it and get guys open. We're best when we kind of mix it up -- point guard shoots, point guard hits the corner, point guard hits me, then I can make the read. That's where I'm best." The game also pits two of the June draft's top seven selections for the first time as professionals. While Memphis' Cameron Boozer and Sacramento's Darius Acuff Jr. have both experienced individual success, only Boozer has an NBA win to his credit. Boozer played a critical role in the Grizzlies' win at Golden State, hitting a go-ahead shot from in the key with 20.1 seconds remaining to cap a 25-point, 13-rebound performance. Ninety miles up the road, meanwhile, Acuff went for 33 points in the Kings' loss to Portland. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sydney's new international airport opens to passengers
item.description: Sydney's new A$5.6 billion ($3.94 billion) airport opened to passengers on Sunday after more than a decade of planning, in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said was a milestone for the country's most populous city.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sydney's new A$5.6 billion ($3.94 billion) airport opened to passengers on Sunday after more than a decade of planning, in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said was a milestone for the country's most populous city. The new Western Sydney International Airport in Badgerys Creek, about 60 km (37.3 miles) west of central Sydney, will operate 24 hours a day, giving [USN:L1N42I00H TEXT:"airlines"] access to a fast-growing and ethnically diverse population centre. The current airport, located closer to Sydney's central business district, can host takeoffs and landings only until 11 p.m. and after 6 a.m., limiting airline scheduling options relative to other major Australian cities like Melbourne. "For the first time in more than 50 years, Australia is opening a major new airport. It’s a milestone that has been decades in the making," Albanese said in a statement. "I’m very proud to officially open it," he said. Qantas' (QAN.AX) budget arm Jetstar was due to operate the first outbound flight to the Gold Coast on Sunday, the airport said in a statement. The airport has capacity for more than 80 million passenger movements annually, it said. The start of passenger services comes after cargo flights commenced at the facility in July. Located on a 1,780-hectare (4,398-acre) site purchased by the federal government in the 1980s, the airport was completed in July 2025 after a seven-year build and 15 years of planning. ($1 = 1.4219 Australian dollars)

item.title: Verstappen's advice to Antonelli: Enjoy the ride and celebrate
item.description: Max Verstappen advised Kimi Antonelli to enjoy the ride and get ready to celebrate as the Italian stands on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Max Verstappen advised Kimi Antonelli to enjoy the ride and get ready to celebrate as the Italian stands on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver [USN:L6N46A08G TEXT:"qualified on pole position"] for Sunday's US Grand Prix and could clinch the title with five rounds to spare, according to the current calendar that includes races in the Middle East, at Austin's Circuit of the Americas if he wins and other results go his way. Red Bull's Verstappen, a four-time champion, will be alongside on the front row and fighting for his third successive victory after Malaysia and Singapore. The Dutch driver will not be making it easy for Antonelli but he also recognised that the main battle was over. "He knows what he's doing, so he just needs to try and win the race. If it (the title) doesn't happen here, it will happen next weekend. If it doesn't happen next weekend, it will happen the weekend after," he said, sitting alongside Antonelli in a post-qualifying press conference. "I think it's just been an incredible season, so you have to also just try and enjoy this kind of ride of the last few months that you've been in. "At one point, of course, it's official, and then you can celebrate probably a little bit." Verstappen said Antonelli, who is 102 points clear of teammate and closest rival George Russell, deserved all the success he was having. "He's very consistent, he's putting the performances in when it matters, and once it's finally official that he is world champion, he's definitely a deserving winner," he said. Antonelli said the weekend did feel different, with his first "match point" in the championship, but the goal remained the same. "We still have to do the race tomorrow, still have to try and win, and then, of course, we'll see what happens. But yeah, I feel like I can enjoy it a bit more because obviously I'm in a very good position," he said. The Italian added that his biggest immediate achievement, on a gusty day with a tailwind blowing, had been to keep his car within the track limits. The Italian has regularly fallen foul of stewards and irritated team boss Toto Wolff with his breaches of the limits this season. "One of the keys was not doing any track limits. That was very good for me because I've had a couple of races where I've done track limits in crucial moments, and that kind of put myself in a bad position and under more pressure. So that hasn't been ideal," he told Sky Sports television.

item.title: Jets, Canadiens face off in Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic
item.description: The Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets will take it outdoors when they meet in the Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg on Sunday evening.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets will take it outdoors when they meet in the Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg on Sunday evening. It will be the NHL's 46th outdoor game and 10th played in Canada. "It's my 11th year and I've never played in (an outdoor game), so I'm really excited," Montreal defenseman Mike Matheson said. "My kids are coming, my wife, my parents. It's going to be a lot of fun. I played in one in college. It's such a different atmosphere and it'll be a lot of fun." The Canadiens are coming in hot, having won two of three, most recently toppling the Chicago Blackhawks 4-1 on Friday. "We want to be winning a lot more hockey games and, to do that, you have to be in a good position in the third," Montreal forward Jake Evans said. "Play a mature game." The Habs played their most recent game without one of its most experienced players, captain Nick Suzuki, who will be out 2-4 weeks because of an upper-body injury. Suzuki did not miss a game in the previous five seasons. Evans stepped up in his absence with two goals and an assist against the Blackhawks, and Matheson added an empty-netter after missing the previous four games with a lower-body injury. "With Nick going down, I think everyone felt like they needed to take another step in their game," Evans said. "It wasn't the prettiest win, I don't think. ... I think we played a smarter game and didn't give them too much." The Jets will be playing their first game since three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner (top goaltender) was traded to the New Jersey Devils on Friday in exchange for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws, a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft, a second-round selection in 2029 and prospect Alexander Command, who was selected 12th overall in the most recent draft. Hellebuyck had been suspended by the Jets for failing to report to training camp after requesting a trade over the summer. "It certainly hasn't been fun, there's no question about it, but at the end of the day, Connor made his choice," Winnipeg general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said on Saturday. "As an organization, we had to act accordingly, and we did." Hellebuyck was introduced to the New Jersey media on Saturday and the 2024-25 NHL MVP brought up Sunday's outdoor game. "There's a lot I need to say, but (the Jets) have the Heritage game coming up," Hellebuyck said. "Out of respect for them and the celebration of hockey, I'm going to postpone that. I hope they know I care about them." Winnipeg has lost four in a row, most recently dropping a 3-2 overtime decision against the Dallas Stars on Thursday. Jets coach Scott Arniel said the most recent performance was an improvement over their 2-1 loss to the St. Louis Blues on the front end of the two-game trip on Tuesday. "We did a lot of better things," Arniel said. "Just, still, some things we got to work on." The Jets also lost some depth on defense when Jack St. Ivany was claimed off waivers by the Washington Capitals on Saturday. --Field Level Media

item.title: North Carolina State dismisses coach Dave Doeren
item.description: North Carolina State fired longtime coach Dave Doeren on Saturday, one day after a 31-28 road loss at Stanford.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Carolina State fired longtime coach Dave Doeren on Saturday, one day after a 31-28 road loss at Stanford. Doeren exits NC State as the winningest coach in school history. He was 98-74 since taking over in 2013. The Wolfpack are 3-4 overall and 1-3 in Atlantic Coast Conference play this season. "I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride," Wolfpack athletic director Boo Corrigan said in a news release. "I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role. We wish Dave, Sara and his family the best in the future." Todd Goebbel, NC State running backs coach/special teams coordinator, will serve as interim coach for the rest of the season. The Wolfpack are beginning an immediate national search for their next coach. Doeren, 54, coached NC State to 10 bowl appearances (4-6 record) and recorded four nine-win seasons. The Wolfpack have just one double-digit victory campaign in their history. That came in 2002 when program legend Philip Rivers led NC State to an 11-3 record under coach Chuck Amato, who died Monday at age 80. This season, NC State beat ACC foe Louisville 31-28 at home and sustained conference losses of 34-8 at Virginia and 38-14 to host Wake Forest. The loss to Stanford marked the fifth time the Wolfpack allowed more than 30 points in a game. Stanford scored on touchdown drives of 84, 86 and 90 yards in the first half and 84 in the second in its Friday night win over the NC State. Doeren also went 23-4 in two seasons at Northern Illinois (2011-12) before taking the NC State job. His overall record is 121-78 in 16 seasons. Goebbel's first game is on Oct. 31 when the Wolfpack host Cal. The 50-year-old has been on the NC State staff since 2019. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bulgaria votes for president in wake of deadly Black Sea drone strikes
item.description: Bulgarians vote in presidential elections on Sunday as Russia's war in Ukraine spreads to the waters off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast.
item.dc:creator: Alex Lefkowitz
item.content:encoded: Bulgarians vote in presidential elections on Sunday as Russia's war in Ukraine spreads to the waters off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. Polls place acting President Iliana Iotova, 61, and ex-caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, as leaders in a race of 27 candidates. While the presidency is largely ceremonial, Sunday's vote has taken on added significance after a [USN:L1N45Z06Q TEXT:"series of drone attacks"] on merchant ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast that likely killed some two-dozen international seafarers. The strikes, which sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine, prompted the government to seek allied assistance to bolster maritime security. Bulgaria has stopped short of directly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks, but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome "benefits the Russian Federation". Both leading presidential candidates condemned the strikes, but they differ over the broader war. Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier. "I want Bulgaria to have a voice of its own in Europe. A reliable NATO ally that defends its interests through preparedness, strong diplomacy and a clear position," he said at a rally on Thursday. Iotova, formerly vice president, became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter the parliamentary race, which he won on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket. Radev supports Iotova and they both call for a diplomatic end to the war. A victory for Iotova would make her Bulgaria's first elected female president. "My opponents argue that there must be a war of attrition." she told a rally on Thursday. "The truth is, we are all the ones who are most exhausted." Polls by Alpha Research give Iotova 41% of the vote and Gyurov 28%. If no candidate wins a majority, a runoff vote will be held on November 1. Voting starts at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) and polls close at 8 p.m.

item.title: Víctimas de abusos aprueban acuerdo de 800 millones de dólares con Arquidiócesis de Nueva York
item.description: Los supervivientes de abusos sexuales por parte del clero llegaron a un acuerdo extrajudicial de 800 millones de dólares con la Arquidiócesis de Nueva York, informaron abogados el sábado, para resolver las demandas presentadas por unas 1.300 personas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los supervivientes de abusos sexuales por parte del clero llegaron a un acuerdo extrajudicial de 800 millones de dólares con la Arquidiócesis de Nueva York, informaron abogados el sábado, para resolver las demandas presentadas por unas 1.300 personas. La Arquidiócesis católica de Nueva York aceptó el pago en mayo, uno de los mayores desembolsos en la oleada de demandas por abusos sexuales por parte del clero en Estados Unidos. El bufete Jeff Anderson & Associates, que representa a 300 supervivientes de abusos, lo calificó como "un momento trascendental en la búsqueda de la justicia". Este acuerdo solo es superado por el de 880 millones de dólares alcanzado por la Arquidiócesis de Los Ángeles en 2024. La Iglesia católica ha pagado miles de millones de dólares en acuerdos en Estados Unidos en los últimos años, después de que Nueva York y otros estados aprobaran leyes que permitían temporalmente a las víctimas de abusos sexuales infantiles presentar demandas por delitos cometidos hace décadas. Además del acuerdo de 800 millones de dólares, la arquidiócesis accedió a hacer públicos documentos relacionados con los agresores sexuales dentro de la Iglesia. El acuerdo también permite a los supervivientes interponer demandas contra las aseguradoras de la Iglesia para obtener indemnizaciones adicionales, pero evita que la arquidiócesis se declare en quiebra.

item.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts drones and missiles as fighting with Yemen's Houthis continues
item.description: Saudi Arabia intercepted drones and missiles over its capital Riyadh and southern areas on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said, as fighting with the Iran-aligned Houthis persisted.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia intercepted drones and missiles over its capital Riyadh and southern areas on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said, as fighting with the Iran-aligned Houthis persisted. The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising front in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran , turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war. On Sunday, Saudi civil defence authorities issued emergency alerts for Riyadh, Abha and Khamis Mushait, before announcing minutes later that the danger had passed. The coalition said two drones and a ballistic missile were launched towards Riyadh, and a cruise missile towards the southern city of Khamis Mushait. It later said it intercepted ten ballistic missiles fired towards southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthis warned they could again target Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday after [USN:S8N44X01H TEXT:"a deadly attack"] earlier this month. The Houthis said they attacked the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the airport remained a "military target" and warned all airlines, airport staffers and travellers against using it. Late on Saturday, the airport said Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers starting Sunday. The airport halted operations on October 10 following an attack - claimed by the Houthis - that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 others, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia has stepped up its strikes against the Houthis after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month, closing in on Bab el-Mandeb Strait - a global maritime chokepoint and shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula to the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed fighting in Yemen has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022. Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of a coalition supporting the internationally recognised government after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa a year earlier.

item.title: Abuse survivors approve $800 million settlement with Archdiocese of New York
item.description: Survivors of clergy sexual abuse have agreed to an $800 million settlement with the Archdiocese of New York, lawyers said on Saturday, to resolve claims brought by approximately 1,300 people.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Survivors of clergy sexual abuse have agreed to an $800 million settlement with the Archdiocese of New York, lawyers said on Saturday, to resolve claims brought by approximately 1,300 people. The Catholic Archdiocese of New York [USN:L1N41E0QA TEXT:"agreed to the payment in May"], one of the largest payouts in a wave of lawsuits over clergy sex abuse in the US. Jeff Anderson & Associates, which represents 300 abuse survivors, called it "a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice." The settlement is second only to an $880 million deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024. The Catholic Church has paid billions of dollars in settlements across the US in the past several years, after New York and other states enacted laws that temporarily enabled victims of child sexual abuse to file lawsuits over decades-old crimes. In addition to the $800 million settlement, the archdiocese agreed to release documents pertaining to sexual offenders in the Church. The settlement also allows survivors to litigate against the Church's insurers for additional payouts, but avoids a bankruptcy by the archdiocese.

item.title: Bodies of ambushed Salvadoran soldiers found in Haiti, New York Times reports
item.description: Four bodies handed over to Salvadoran forces on Saturday do not belong to the four soldiers who had been ambushed the previous Sunday outside the capital of Haiti, El Salvador President Nayib Bukele said, contradicting a New York Times report.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Four bodies handed over to Salvadoran forces on Saturday do not belong to the four soldiers who had been ambushed the previous Sunday outside the capital of Haiti, El Salvador President Nayib Bukele said, contradicting a New York Times report. "They are not our men," Bukele said in a post on X, hours after The New York Times reported that the bodies had been found and were believed to be those of the Salvadoran soldiers. The four went missing on Sunday after they jumped from a burning armored vehicle that came under attack on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince while they were returning from a market to their base. Bukele said the four bodies handed over included a child, a man much taller than the Salvadorans and a soldier from another country. He shared photos of a soldier's identification from Chad. The ambush was the first major attack on the Gang Suppression Force, a UN-authorized multinational mission, since it began operations in Haiti this year. The international security mission declined to comment on the matter. Earlier this week, Bukele said gangs were holding the four men and that El Salvador had launched a military operation to bring them back unharmed. Additional Salvadoran troops were later deployed to support search and security operations. No group has publicly claimed responsibility for the attack. Local media have linked the ambush to gangs operating in the area, including powerful armed groups Chen Mechan and 400 Mawozo. A year into its mandate, the GSF has about 2,000 troops on the ground, well below its authorized ceiling of 5,500. An earlier Kenyan-led security effort struggled with chronic shortages of money, equipment and personnel. Haiti's gangs have expanded sharply since the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise, taking control of large parts of Port-au-Prince and displacing 1.4 million to 1.5 million people.

item.title: Los cuerpos hallados en Haití no pertenecen a los soldados salvadoreños emboscados: Bukele
item.description: Los cuatro cuerpos entregados a las fuerzas salvadoreñas el sábado —que inicialmente se creía que correspondían a cuatro soldados emboscados en las afueras de la capital de Haití— no pertenecen a los uniformados desaparecidos, dijo el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los cuatro cuerpos entregados a las fuerzas salvadoreñas el sábado —que inicialmente se creía que correspondían a cuatro soldados emboscados en las afueras de la capital de Haití— no pertenecen a los uniformados desaparecidos, dijo el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele. "No son nuestros hombres", afirmó Bukele en una publicación en X. Previamente, The New York Times había informado el sábado sobre el hallazgo de los cuerpos, señalando que se creía que eran los de los soldados salvadoreños. Los cuatro militares desaparecieron el domingo pasado tras saltar de un vehículo blindado en llamas que fue atacado en las afueras de Puerto Príncipe, mientras regresaban a su base desde un mercado. Bukele indicó que entre los cuatro cuerpos entregados se encontraban un niño, un hombre de una "estatura considerablemente mayor" a la de los soldados salvadoreños, y un militar de otro país; al respecto, compartió fotografías de la identificación de un soldado proveniente de Chad. La emboscada constituye el primer ataque de gran envergadura contra la Fuerza de Supresión de Pandillas —una misión multinacional autorizada por las Naciones Unidas— desde que comenzó sus operaciones en Haití este año. La misión de seguridad internacional declinó hacer comentarios al respecto. A principios de la semana, Bukele había señalado que los cuatro hombres estaban retenidos por pandillas y que El Salvador había puesto en marcha una operación militar para rescatarlos ilesos. Posteriormente, se desplegaron más tropas salvadoreñas para reforzar las labores de búsqueda y seguridad. Ningún grupo ha reivindicado públicamente la autoría del ataque. Medios locales han vinculado la emboscada con pandillas que operan en la zona, entre ellas los poderosos grupos armados "Chen Mechan" y "400 Mawozo". A un año del inicio de su mandato, la Fuerza de Supresión de Pandillas cuenta con unos 2.000 efectivos sobre el terreno, una cifra muy inferior al límite autorizado de 5500. Un esfuerzo de seguridad previo, liderado por Kenia, enfrentó carencias crónicas de fondos, equipamiento y personal. Las pandillas en Haití han extendido su control de manera significativa desde el asesinato del presidente Jovenel Moïse en 2021, apoderándose de amplias zonas de Puerto Príncipe y provocando el desplazamiento de entre 1,4 y 1,5 millones de personas.

item.title: Antonelli logra la pole para el Gran Premio de EEUU con el título de F1 a la vista
item.description: Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, saldrá desde la pole position en un Gran Premio de Estados Unidos que podría convertirlo en el campeón del mundo más joven de la Fórmula 1 si los resultados le son favorables el domingo.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, saldrá desde la pole position en un Gran Premio de Estados Unidos que podría convertirlo en el campeón del mundo más joven de la Fórmula 1 si los resultados le son favorables el domingo. Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, acompañará al italiano de 20 años en la primera fila tras la sesión de clasificación del sábado en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin. Su compañero de equipo, Isack Hadjar, quedó tercero, y Charles Leclerc, de Ferrari, completará la segunda fila. Antonelli cuenta con una ventaja de 102 puntos en el campeonato sobre George Russell, su rival más cercano y compañero de equipo, que se clasificó sexto. Aún quedarán 125 puntos por disputar tras la carrera del domingo. Para hacerse con el título, el italiano tendrá que ganar, mientras que Russell y el siete veces campeón de Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, no deben terminar por encima del noveno y el quinto puesto, respectivamente. Hamilton se clasificó quinto tras marcar el mejor tiempo en la última sesión de entrenamientos. La pole fue la primera de Antonelli desde Bélgica en julio. "Hemos conseguido la pole, así que intentaremos ganar mañana", dijo el italiano en declaraciones al público tras salir del coche. "Max ha estado muy rápido e Isack ha hecho un trabajo increíble, así que no será fácil".

item.title: Packers activate RB Josh Jacobs to play vs. Lions
item.description: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was activated Saturday after missing the first six games while on the commissioner's exempt list and is set to make his season debut on Sunday against the Detroit Lions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was activated Saturday after missing the first six games while on the commissioner's exempt list and is set to make his season debut on Sunday against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs was on the exempt list after pleading no-contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and destruction of property on Sept. 10. The charges were related to an incident with a then-girlfriend on May 23 at Jacobs' home near Green Bay. The NFL removed Jacobs from the exempt list on Monday. Jacobs could still receive further penalties as the NFL has a pending personal-conduct investigation ongoing. Jacobs, 28, addressed his situations with reporters on Wednesday. "I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character," Jacobs said. "I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lot of people that know me in this locker room or that's been around me, I'll let them do that. But for me, man, I'm just trying to come back in here and play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward." Jacobs is in his eighth NFL season and third with the Packers. Last year, he gained 929 yards on 234 carries (4.0 average) with 13 touchdowns. The three-time Pro Bowl honoree led the NFL in rushing yards in 2022 with 1,653 for the Las Vegas Raiders. In 105 career games (104 starts), Jacobs has produced 7,803 yards on 1,840 carries (4.2 average) with 74 touchdowns. Green Bay also signed receiver/returner Coleman Owen from the practice squad, elevated edge rusher Arron Mosby from the practice squad and activated defensive tackle Jordon Riley off the physically unable to perform list. --Field Level Media

item.title: Detenciones en Barcelona tras marchas antisistema en los que alborotadores saquean tiendas, provocan incendios
item.description: Un total de 100 personas fueron detenidas en Barcelona el sábado por la noche después de que manifestantes encapuchados que participaban en una manifestación antisistema saquearan tiendas e incendiaran mobiliario urbano en los alrededores de la céntrica Plaza de Cataluña.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un total de 100 personas fueron detenidas en Barcelona el sábado por la noche después de que manifestantes encapuchados que participaban en una manifestación antisistema saquearan tiendas e incendiaran mobiliario urbano en los alrededores de la céntrica Plaza de Cataluña. Núria Parlon, consejera de Interior de la comunidad autónoma de Cataluña, afirmó que alrededor del 25% de los detenidos eran menores. Añadió que se provocaron más de 30 incendios y que 14 tiendas fueron destrozadas o saqueadas en una zona de la ciudad muy frecuentada por turistas. En publicaciones en redes sociales se convocaba a los manifestantes a un movimiento "contra el sistema". Las publicaciones también utilizaban el lema "Institut Indignats", una traducción del movimiento "Lyceés Indignés", que se empleó para movilizar a los estudiantes que han protestado en Francia en las últimas semanas. Videos difundidos en las redes sociales muestran a personas atrapadas en el interior de tiendas, entre ellas los grandes almacenes El Corte Inglés, después de que se bajaran las persianas para evitar los saqueos. Otras publicaciones mostraban a manifestantes encapuchados y vestidos de negro rompiendo escaparates a patadas y llevándose mercancía, en algunos casos animados por los espectadores en línea.

item.title: Flávio tem 50,8% dos votos válidos e Lula está com 49,2%, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com vantagem numérica para o senador de oposição, mostrou pesquisa Atlas/Bloomberg neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão em empate técnico na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com vantagem numérica para o senador de oposição, mostrou pesquisa Atlas/Bloomberg neste sábado. Flávio tem 50,8% dos votos válidos, quando não são computados os votos brancos, nulos e os indecisos, contra 49,2% de Lula. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 1 ponto percentual para mais ou para menos. Considerando as intenções de voto totais, o senador soma 49,9% contra 48,4% do presidente, segundo a pesquisa deste sábado. No levantamento anterior, no início da semana, o placar era de 49,8% a 47,6% a favor de Flávio. Os que disseram que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou estão indecisos somam 1,7%, ante 2,6%. Para a pesquisa, contratada pela Bloomberg, o instituto AtlasIntel ouviu 4.990 pessoas online entre os dias 18 e 23 de outubro.

item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão empatados tecnicamente na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) estão empatados tecnicamente na véspera do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado. Nos votos válidos não são computados os brancos, nulos e os indecisos. No primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, Flávio terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula.
